Introduction

介绍

It is very satisfying to observe an organization having achieved Operational Excellence. The managers are focused, working on the tasks where they have the most leverage; long are gone the days where they were running all over the place fixing emergencies. The workers are proud of their work, each owning his role and trusting his manager. The workplace is a good environment to work in: little dangers, everything is at its place, everyone knows what the company is doing and cares about it.

看到一个组织实现卓越运营，令人非常欣慰。管理人员目标明确，专注于他们最擅长的任务；他们不再像以前那样疲于奔命地处理各种突发状况。员工们为自己的工作感到自豪，每个人都对自己的职责负责，并且信任自己的经理。工作场所环境良好：安全隐患少，一切井然有序，每个人都了解公司的运作并关心公司的发展。

Unfortunately, Operational Excellence is being practiced in few companies only, for two reasons. First, few managers know how to achieve it. And second, most managers do not have it as their priority. While they are interested in the benefits of Operational Excellence, they are not convinced that such benefits are worth the efforts required to achieve them.

遗憾的是，卓越运营目前仅在少数公司得到实践，原因有二。首先，很少有管理者知道如何实现卓越运营。其次，大多数管理者并未将其视为优先事项。尽管他们对卓越运营的益处感兴趣，但他们并不认为这些益处值得付出相应的努力。

There are many selfish reasons to implement Operational Excellence. Managers of a team with a culture of Operational Excellence are less stressed (they do not spend their days running after emergencies), work less hours (when you are effective, you don’t have to work overtime), are more fulfilled (they become respected by both their subordinates and their boss), are more valuable (they and their team become able to consistently hit milestones), are more employable (being able to manage a team effectively is a rare and valuable skill), and are richer (as their team hits their bottom line results, more money becomes available to be distributed in the form of bonuses).

实施卓越运营有很多利己的理由。拥有卓越运营文化的团队管理者压力更小（他们不必整天疲于奔命地应对突发事件），工作时间更短（高效运营无需加班），更有成就感（他们赢得下属和上级的尊重），更有价值（他们和团队能够持续达成里程碑），更受雇主青睐（有效管理团队是一项稀缺且宝贵的技能），也更富有（随着团队达成业绩目标，更多资金可以以奖金的形式发放）。

Achieving Operational Excellence is not complex. It does take a limited amount of focused effort, but the benefits begin to show very fast, if you know what to focus on.

实现卓越运营并不复杂。虽然需要投入少量精力，但只要知道应该关注什么，就能很快看到成效。

The first part of this book provides solutions to the problem: what to focus on. It will tell you which actions matter and which do not, so that you won’t waste your time and energy on things which will not bring you any good. It will show you which are the few actions that, if taken, will have a disproportionate impact on your working life.

本书第一部分旨在解决“应该关注什么”这个问题。它会告诉你哪些行动重要，哪些无关紧要，从而避免你把时间和精力浪费在无益的事情上。它还会指出，哪些行动一旦采取，将对你的工作生活产生巨大的积极影响。

The second part of this book provides you with Eight Best Practices: quick tools you can begin using today to change the way your team operates and to get evidence that things can change: unmotivated employees can become motivated, unproductive ones can become productive, and previously unreachable objectives can be attained.

本书第二部分为您提供八项最佳实践：您可以立即开始使用的快速工具，以改变团队的运作方式，并获得改变的证据：缺乏动力的员工可以变得有动力，效率低下的员工可以变得高效，以前无法实现的目标可以实现。

In the third and last part of this book, you will find a roadmap to extend the change to scopes larger than your direct subordinates. For example, your plant, your office or your organization.

本书第三部分也是最后一部分，将提供一份路线图，指导您将变革的范围扩展到超出您直接下属的范围，例如您的工厂、办公室或组织。

I’ve been working in the field of Operational Excellence for more than seven years and, while it might not seem much, I’ve seen hundreds of companies and consulted dozens. I’ve witnessed problems and solutions. I know what works and what doesn’t. This book is the result: a practical guide to help you becoming a more effective manager and to solve most of your problems at work.

我在卓越运营领域工作了七年多，虽然时间不长，但我接触过数百家公司，也为数十家公司提供过咨询服务。我见证过各种各样的问题和解决方案。我知道哪些方法有效，哪些无效。这本书就是我总结的经验：一本实用的指南，旨在帮助您成为更高效的管理者，并解决工作中遇到的大部分问题。

Achieving Operational Excellence

实现卓越运营

Operational Excellence is not an abstract concept which lives in the theories of academics. Operational Excellence is what happens on the work floor, on the production lines and in the warehouses. How employees work when they are actively supervised and when they aren’t. On the good days and, especially, on the bad ones, when everyone is tired or rushed.

卓越运营并非存在于学术理论中的抽象概念。它体现在工作现场、生产线和仓库中。它关乎员工在受到积极监督和缺乏监督时的工作方式，关乎顺境和逆境，尤其是在每个人都疲惫不堪或匆忙赶工的时候。

Achieving Operational Excellence is not a complex endeavor. A few right actions applied with enough consistency are enough to turn a company’s operations around in just a few months, as I’ve witnessed with my own eyes in the companies I worked with. However, this is not easy. The difficulty in achieving Operational Excellence is not in the know-how required for it to happen, but in getting the time, systems and proactivity needed by the managers to transform the Four Principles of Operational Excellence into concrete actions that will change the way workers operate. This book will help you with this.

实现卓越运营并非难事。正如我在曾共事的公司亲眼所见，只要采取一些正确的措施并持之以恒，就能在短短几个月内扭转公司的运营局面。然而，这并非易事。实现卓越运营的难点不在于所需的专业知识，而在于管理者如何获得所需的时间、系统和积极性，从而将卓越运营的四大原则转化为切实可行的行动，改变员工的工作方式。本书将助您一臂之力。

But first, let me begin with a story of change.

但首先，让我从一个关于变革的故事开始。

…

At the crossroad of the 17 th and the 18 th century, a French chemist by the name of Éleuthère Irénée du Pont had to leave the country in a hurry. He had been a student of renowned chemist Lavoisier, but things recently changed. Due to political controversies following the French revolution, to escape jail and, perhaps, the guillotine, Éleuthère du Pont took a boat and sailed to the New Continent.

在17世纪末18世纪初，一位名叫埃勒泰尔·伊雷内·杜邦的法国化学家不得不匆匆离开法国。他曾是著名化学家拉瓦锡的学生，但不久之后，情况发生了变化。由于法国大革命后的政治纷争，为了逃避牢狱之灾，甚至可能免于断头台的命运，埃勒泰尔·杜邦乘船远航至新大陆。

On the 1 st of January 1800, he landed in Delaware. Equipped with his chemical know-how, he began operating a gunpowder factory on the shores of the Brandywine River. As he would soon learn, gunpowder factories have an undesirable property: they tend to explode frequently.

1800年1月1日，他抵达特拉华州。凭借着化学方面的知识，他在白兰地河畔开办了一家火药厂。他很快就会发现，火药厂有一个不好的特性：它们很容易发生爆炸。

Facing increased incidents, injuries and deaths, he decided something had to be done to reduce the explosions. How he solved the problem shaped the future of Operational Excellence.

面对日益增多的事故、伤亡，他意识到必须采取措施减少爆炸。他解决问题的方式塑造了卓越运营的未来。

Éleuthère du Pont took two initiatives [1] . First, he required that the Director (himself) lived inside the factory with his family. He put his life on the line. If something blew up, he and his family might die in the process. Skin in the game.

埃勒特尔·杜邦采取了两项举措[1]。首先，他要求厂长（他本人）与家人一起住在工厂里。他把自己的生命置于危险之中。如果发生爆炸，他和他的家人都可能丧命。这是切身利益攸关。

Second, he established the rule that every new machinery had to be operated for the first time by members of top management. If the machine blew up, the manager would suffer the consequences on his own skin.

其次，他制定了一条规定：所有新机器都必须由高层管理人员首次操作。如果机器发生爆炸，经理将承担全部责任。

Needless to say, the safety of the plant increased overnight. Leadership demonstrated through visible costly actions is powerful.

毋庸置疑，工厂的安全状况一夜之间得到了提升。以看得见摸得着的代价换来的领导力是强有力的。

The gunpowder company slowly grew into one of the largest industrial conglomerates in the world, DuPont. Its destiny would eventually cross mine two centuries later.

这家火药公司逐渐发展成为世界上最大的工业集团之一——杜邦公司。两个世纪后，它的命运最终与我的命运交织在了一起。

…

Even though I graduated as an automotive engineer, I never worked as one. On a hot summer day in which I was writing my final thesis, I received a call from who would become my first boss. He asked me to join his consulting team in Frankfurt, Germany. Excited and without knowing a single word of German, I accepted. I became an employee of DuPont [2] .

虽然我大学毕业时拿到的是汽车工程学位，但我从未从事过相关工作。在一个炎热的夏日，我正在撰写毕业论文，突然接到一个电话，对方就是我未来的第一位老板。他邀请我加入他在德国法兰克福的咨询团队。我当时既兴奋又不懂德语，但还是接受了邀请。我成为了杜邦公司的员工[2]。

While there, I learned a lot. At the time, DuPont was considered the leading world expert in Workplace Safety consulting. I had the chance to work with some of the top experts on this planet. I saw tens of companies: our clients. I learned from hundreds of managers, and thousands of workers. I listened to their words, their problems and their aspirations. I experienced their best practices. I analyzed failures. I came up with solutions. I followed their implementation. I internalized Operational Excellence.

在那里，我学到了很多。当时，杜邦公司被公认为是全球领先的工作场所安全咨询专家。我有幸与一些世界顶尖的专家共事。我走访了数十家公司：我们的客户。我向数百位经理和数千名员工学习。我倾听他们的心声，了解他们的问题和愿景。我学习了他们的最佳实践。我分析了失败案例。我提出了解决方案。我跟踪了解决方案的实施情况。我真正理解了卓越运营的精髓。

A few years later, I left to start my own consulting practice. I spent some months reading as much as possible about Operational Excellence, learning as much as I could and talking with old experts and new clients. Then, I developed a framework to help any manager improving the Operational Culture of his company.

几年后，我离开公司，开始了自己的咨询事业。我花了几个月的时间，尽可能多地阅读有关卓越运营的书籍，尽可能多地学习，并与资深专家和新客户交流。之后，我开发了一套框架，旨在帮助任何管理者改善其公司的运营文化。

I now run my own consulting practice, helping managers (mostly in Europe and Asia) developing their employees and running their operations to the best of their potential.

我现在经营自己的咨询公司，帮助管理者（主要在欧洲和亚洲）培养员工，并最大限度地发挥其运营潜力。

However, helping managers one-by-one limits my leverage. I can only help so many people face-to-face. I needed to find a way to impact more people. Therefore, I decided to write this book.

然而，一对一地帮助管理者会限制我的影响力。我能面对面帮助的人毕竟有限。我需要找到一种能够影响更多人的方法。因此，我决定写这本书。

Outline

大纲

This book is divided into three parts.

本书分为三个部分。

In the first part, you will learn the Four Principles of Operational Excellence to be leveraged in order to create an Operational Culture worth working in.

在第一部分中，您将学习卓越运营的四个原则，以便利用这些原则来创建值得为之工作的运营文化。

In the second part, I will detail the Eight Best Practices to transform the Four Principles into visible actions, which you can carry out starting today in your organization. I will provide detailed lists of steps and comprehensive examples to facilitate their execution.

在第二部分，我将详细介绍八项最佳实践，帮助您将四大原则转化为切实可行的行动，您可以从今天开始在您的组织中实施这些行动。我将提供详细的步骤清单和全面的示例，以帮助您顺利完成这些行动。

In the third part, I will provide you with a roadmap for planning a plant-wide or company-wide change initiative, for achieving Top Management buy-in, for its effective roll-out and for its long-term sustenance .

在第三部分，我将为您提供一份路线图，用于规划全厂或全公司范围的变革计划，以获得高层管理人员的支持，有效推广并长期维持。

But first, let’s take a look at the importance of Operational Excellence and at the costs of a mediocre Operational Culture.

但首先，让我们来看看卓越运营的重要性以及平庸的运营文化所带来的代价。

Operational Excellence and management

卓越运营与管理

The first part of this book – the Four Principles of Operational Excellence – talks about management, not about best practices, which are the subject of the second part. This is necessary, as no best practice will be followed by the employees of your organization, if the managers are not able to do their job of setting clear personal objectives and holding them accountable in a fair, transparent and predictable manner.

本书第一部分——卓越运营的四大原则——探讨的是管理，而非最佳实践，最佳实践是第二部分的主题。这是必要的，因为如果管理者无法履行职责，设定清晰的个人目标，并以公平、透明和可预测的方式追究员工的责任，那么组织中的员工就无法遵循任何最佳实践。

I would urge you to give your maximum attention to the first part of this book, even if you feel you already know about management, as the concepts contained here are not the usual boilerplate and not having internalized them is the real bottleneck to Operational Excellence. Looking for one more best practice to implement while you do not have a solid foundation of performance management will only bring short-lived satisfaction. The real changes in your working life will come from mastering The Four Principles.

即使您自认为对管理有所了解，我也强烈建议您认真阅读本书的第一部分，因为其中阐述的概念并非老生常谈，而未能真正理解和掌握这些概念才是实现卓越运营的真正瓶颈。如果您在绩效管理方面缺乏扎实的基础，却盲目地寻找新的最佳实践来实施，只会带来短暂的满足感。真正改变您职业生涯的，唯有掌握这四大原则。

A map

地图

When you look at a map describing the roads in your city, you do not see every single building and every single tree. Not describing the full territory is not a defect of maps, but a feature. By leaving out some details, they allow the reader to focus on the information present and to take effective action.

当你查看城市道路地图时，你不会看到每一栋建筑和每一棵树。地图不涵盖所有区域并非缺陷，而是其特点。通过省略一些细节，地图可以让读者专注于已有的信息，从而采取有效的行动。

Similarly, this book does not pretend to explain everything there is to know about Operational Excellence – it would take a hundred books to do so. Rather, this book describes most of what you need to know in order to be able to take effective action to improve the Operational Culture of your team.

同样，本书也并非旨在解释卓越运营的方方面面——这需要一百本书才能做到。相反，本书着重介绍您需要了解的大部分内容，以便采取有效措施来改善团队的运营文化。

If you have any question whose answer is not contained in this book, you can always drop me a short [3] email at the contact listed in the author section at the end of this book.

如果您有任何本书中没有解答的问题，您可以随时通过本书末尾作者部分列出的联系方式给我发一封简短的电子邮件[3]。

Terminology

术语

In this book, I use the following definitions for roles: “Worker” refers to any employee who does not manage any subordinate, “Supervisor” refers to any employee who manages workers, “Manager” refers to any employee who manages subordinates of any kind (workers, supervisors or other managers) and “Top Management” refers to the CEO and other top executives such as C-suites and Vice-Presidents.

本书中，我对角色使用了以下定义：“员工”指不管理任何下属的员工，“主管”指管理员工的员工，“经理”指管理任何类型的下属（员工、主管或其他经理）的员工，“高层管理人员”指首席执行官和其他高层管理人员，如首席高管和副总裁。

Unless specified otherwise, by “subordinates” I intend those who report directly to person being referred to. For example, “your subordinates” would include your direct reports, but not your reports’ reports, if any.

除非另有说明，我所说的“下属”是指直接向被提及人汇报的人员。例如，“您的下属”包括您的直接下属，但不包括您的下属的下属（如有）。

The Costs of Lacking Operational Excellence

缺乏卓越运营的代价

Achieving and maintaining a great Operational Culture costs time and money. However, such investments are cheap compared to the costs of a mediocre Operational Culture, plagued by structural problems, demotivated employees and lack of clarity and trust.

建立和维护卓越的运营文化需要投入时间和金钱。然而，与平庸的运营文化相比，这些投资是微不足道的。平庸的运营文化往往饱受结构性问题、员工士气低落以及缺乏清晰度和信任等问题的困扰。

Let’s first see the costs for managers like you.

我们先来看看像您这样的管理者需要付出哪些成本。

  • Overtime: in companies with mediocre Operational Culture, action is slow and problems aren’t addressed without constant attention by the manager. In companies with great Operational Culture, instead, there is no need for micromanagement, and managers are more likely to (and are encouraged to) leave their work on time most of their days.
    加班：在运营文化平庸的公司里，行动迟缓，问题需要管理者持续关注才能解决。相反，在运营文化优秀的公司里，无需微观管理，管理者更有可能（并且也被鼓励）在大多数日子里准时下班。
  • Lower bonuses: teams with mediocre Operational Culture fail to achieve their business goals or bring minimum impact to the bottom line. Instead, teams with great Operational Culture effectively contribute to the success of the company, which has then the funds and the reasons to distribute large bonuses or raises.
    较低的奖金：运营文化平庸的团队无法实现业务目标，或对公司盈利贡献甚微。相反，运营文化优秀的团队能够有效地为公司成功做出贡献，公司也就有资金和理由发放高额奖金或加薪。
  • More stress: it is stressful to work in a team with mediocre Operational Culture, where new and old problems surface every day. Instead, teams with great Operational Culture take care of problems once and for all, allowing their members to work in an environment mostly deprived of toxic stress.
    压力更大：在运营文化平庸的团队中工作压力巨大，因为新问题和老问题每天都会涌现。相反，拥有卓越运营文化的团队能够一劳永逸地解决问题，让成员们在一个几乎没有有害压力的环境中工作。
  • Less energy: managers of teams with mediocre Operational Culture spend their days “putting out fires”, running from one place to another solving urgent problems, an activity which would quickly deplete anyone’s reserves of energy. Instead, in teams with great Operational Culture, problems are solved by individual team members, leaving the manager free to work on a few important problems rather than on many urgent ones.
    精力不足：运营文化平庸的团队管理者整天疲于奔命，疲于奔命地解决各种紧急问题，这种奔波会迅速耗尽任何人的精力。相反，在运营文化优秀的团队中，问题由团队成员自行解决，管理者可以腾出精力处理少数重要问题，而不是疲于应对众多紧急事务。
  • Less trust: in teams with mediocre Operational Culture, career advancements are based at least partially on factors other than results. Behaviors such as servility, adulation and backstabbing go unpunished at best and are rewarded at worst, creating an environment where it is impossible to trust most colleagues. Conversely, in teams with great Operational Excellence, people are rewarded to act in accordance to Core Values and objectives – both defined in objective terms – and punished if they exhibit any toxic behavior. The result is an environment where everyone can trust each other.
    信任度较低：在运营文化平庸的团队中，职业晋升至少部分取决于业绩以外的因素。谄媚、奉承和背后捅刀等行为，往好了说不会受到惩罚，往坏了说反而会得到奖励，从而营造出一种同事之间互不信任的氛围。相反，在运营卓越团队中，员工会因践行核心价值观和目标（两者都以客观标准定义）而获得奖励，任何不良行为都会受到惩罚。最终，团队会营造出一种人人互信的氛围。
  • Less satisfaction: for all the reasons above, to work in a team with mediocre Operational Culture is consuming, tiring, stressing, and not worth it financially. Instead, working for a team with great Operational Culture is rewarding, both from the financial and the mental point of view.
    满意度降低：综上所述，在运营文化平庸的团队中工作会让人精疲力竭、压力巨大，而且在经济上得不偿失。相反，在运营文化优秀的团队中工作则会带来丰厚的回报，无论从经济角度还是精神角度来看都是如此。

Just like a mediocre Operational Culture is bad for managers, it is also expensive for companies. These are the direct costs of lacking Operational Excellence:

平庸的运营文化不仅对管理者不利，对公司而言也代价高昂。以下是缺乏卓越运营的直接成本：

  • Defects, which lead to scrap, rework, customer support and recalls.
    缺陷会导致报废、返工、客户支持和产品召回。
  • Poor logistics, which lead to transportation, storage and capital immobilization costs which do not add any value to the customer.
    物流不畅导致运输、仓储和资金占用成本，而这些成本并未给客户带来任何价值。
  • Injuries, which lead to stopped production and worker benefits.
    工伤事故会导致生产停滞和工人福利损失。
  • Environmental problems, which lead to fines.
    环境问题会导致罚款。
  • Unethical workplaces, which lead to fines, rogue employees and key personnel being fired for ethical violations.
    不道德的工作场所会导致罚款、不守规矩的员工以及因违反道德规范而被解雇的关键人员。

These direct costs are dwarfed by indirect ones:

这些直接成本与间接成本相比简直微不足道：

  • Defects lead to brand issues, making it more expensive to acquire and retain customers.
    缺陷会导致品牌问题，增加获取和留住客户的成本。
  • Poor logistics lead to stopped production in case of delays in the supply line, in unhappy customers or in customers having to source another supplier (a competitor of yours) to protect themselves from your delays.
    物流不畅会导致供应链延误，进而导致生产停滞、客户不满，或者客户为了避免受到你的延误影响而不得不寻找其他供应商（你的竞争对手）。
  • Injuries lead to poorer quality and operations (as less experienced workers have to substitute for injured ones), lower morale and higher insurance costs.
    工伤会导致质量和运营效率下降（因为经验不足的工人不得不代替受伤的工人），士气低落，保险成本上升。
  • Environmental problems lead to brand incidents (damaging the image customers and potential hires have of the company) and risk of losing the permit to operate.
    环境问题会导致品牌事件（损害客户和潜在员工对公司的印象），并有失去经营许可证的风险。
  • Unethical workplaces lead to brand incidents, difficulties in hiring and retaining talent (most people do not want to work for a company with a poor work environment and must be overpaid to do so).
    不道德的工作场所会导致品牌事件，以及招聘和留住人才的困难（大多数人都不愿意为工作环境差的公司工作，必须支付过高的薪水才会这样做）。
  • Poor management leads to employees having a lower morale and motivation, underperforming in all other areas, and key employees leaving the company.
    管理不善会导致员工士气低落、积极性下降，在其他各个方面表现不佳，以及关键员工离开公司。

Summing it up, companies with poor Operational Culture lose their good employees (to injuries, burnouts, competitors) and remain with bad employees only (low-talent or unethical ones), which further lowers the Operational Culture, creating a vicious circle from which it is difficult to exit.

总而言之，运营文化差的公司会失去优秀的员工（因伤病、倦怠、被竞争对手挖走），只留下差劲的员工（能力低下或不道德的员工），这会进一步降低运营文化，形成难以摆脱的恶性循环。

For all the reasons listed above, it is beneficial both to managers and companies to strive to implement Operational Excellence in their organization.

鉴于以上所有原因，努力在组织中实施卓越运营对管理者和公司都是有益的。

Let’s see how.

我们来看看具体怎么做。

# ↩

Managing difficult employees

管理难缠的员工

Before entering the core of this book and describe the Four Principles of Operational Excellence and the Eight Best Practices to implement them in your organization, let’s explore three problems most managers like you face: managing difficult employees, getting the time to do everything and creating an environment of trust. They’re not an exhaustive list of course – there are more urgent and more important problems – but these are the three problems which will be covered as the introduction to the core of this book: the Four Principles of Operational Excellence.

在深入探讨本书的核心内容，介绍卓越运营的四大原则以及在您的组织中实施这些原则的八项最佳实践之前，让我们先来探讨一下大多数像您一样的管理者都会面临的三个问题：管理难缠的员工、如何安排时间完成所有工作以及如何营造信任的氛围。当然，这并非全部问题——还有更紧迫、更重要的问题——但这三个问题将作为本书核心内容——卓越运营的四大原则——的引言进行阐述。

By “difficult employees”, I refer to those who appear to chronically lack any motivation, to those who seem to resist any attempt to change their ways of working, to those who have adversarial reactions to attempts to train them, or to those who lack the discipline required to work in a team.

我所说的“难缠的员工”是指那些长期缺乏动力、抗拒任何改变工作方式的尝试、对培训尝试抱有抵触情绪，或者缺乏团队合作所需纪律的员工。

The reason why these four seemingly different groups are classified under the same umbrella is that they have a common root cause: the employee does not know that good individual outcomes follow achieving objectives (or he forgot about it, or got taught otherwise by working under bad managers, or believes that it is not true in your company or under your management).

之所以将这四个看似不同的群体归为同一类，是因为它们有一个共同的根本原因：员工不知道良好的个人结果会随着目标的实现而到来（或者他忘记了这一点，或者在糟糕的管理者手下工作时被灌输了错误的观念，或者认为这在你的公司或你的管理下是不成立的）。

In some cases, the employee never got to learn the link between achieving objectives and good individual outcomes because he has always lacked the skills to do the former or because he only encountered teachers and managers in his life who never rewarded him with the latter. In other cases, the employee happened to spend the last months or years working for a manager who failed to set any attainable objective, or who failed to provide him with the skills and supports required to achieve it, or who was inconsistent in rewarding him for having achieved his objectives, to the point that the employee forgot that achieving objectives is followed by good individual outcomes.

在某些情况下，员工从未有机会了解达成目标与良好个人业绩之间的联系，因为他一直缺乏实现目标所需的技能，或者因为他一生中遇到的老师和管理者从未给予他良好的个人业绩奖励。在另一些情况下，员工在过去的几个月或几年里，恰巧为一位未能设定任何可实现目标、未能提供达成目标所需的技能和支持、或者在奖励方面前后矛盾的管理者工作，以至于员工忘记了达成目标会带来良好的个人业绩。

In a few cases, the root cause is instead that the employee did not get to learn the link between doing something bad and bad individual outcomes. This happens when the employee, for any reason – at work, or in his early years at school – did something which was bad, did not get punished and reaped benefits instead. For example, the employee might have been arriving late at meetings and experienced no material consequence, thus learning that bad behavior goes unpunished.

在少数情况下，根本原因在于员工没有机会认识到不良行为与不良个人后果之间的联系。这种情况发生在员工无论出于何种原因——无论是在工作中还是在早期求学阶段——做了不好的事情，却没有受到惩罚，反而从中获益。例如，员工可能经常开会迟到，但没有受到任何实质性的惩罚，从而形成了“不良行为不会受到惩罚”的观念。

The root causes of difficult employees

难缠员工的根本原因

Problem

问题

Consequence

结果

They never got to achieve any objective

他们从未实现任何目标。

They did not experience that achieving objectives leads to positive individual outcomes

他们没有体验到实现目标会带来积极的个人结果。

After achieving objectives, they didn’t get to experience the rewards

达成目标后，他们却没能享受到奖励。

They now believe that achieving objectives is not necessarily followed by positive individual outcomes.

他们现在认为，实现目标并不一定会带来积极的个人结果。

After failing to achieve objectives, they still get to enjoy benefits as if they did achieve them

即使未能实现目标，他们仍然可以享受如同实现目标一样的利益。

They now believe that productive behavior is unnecessary.

他们现在认为，生产性行为是不必要的。

In rare cases, there are other reasons underlying underperformance or bad behaviors, but the reasons listed above cover the large majority.

在极少数情况下，表现不佳或不良行为背后可能还有其他原因，但以上列举的原因涵盖了绝大多数情况。

Difficult employees behave as such because they experienced a paradigm where bad behavior is more advantageous than productive behavior.

难管教的员工之所以表现如此，是因为他们曾经经历过一种不良行为比良好行为更有利的模式。

The solution, therefore, is simple (though hard): the manager should let them experience a different paradigm, where bad behavior consistently leads to negative individual outcomes and good behavior consistently leads to positive individual outcomes.

因此，解决办法很简单（虽然很难）：管理者应该让他们体验一种不同的模式，在这种模式下，不良行为会持续导致负面的个人结果，而良好行为会持续导致正面的个人结果。

The key word is consistently . It’s not that most managers do not reward achieving objectives. They do. However, often, they do it less consistently that they let having achieved objectives go unrewarded. Unfortunately, people are more likely to remember that one time where their efforts went to waste rather than those nine times where they got rewarded. Unless the manager is obsessively consistent in making sure that the consequences he promises (both good and bad) take place, his words will not command attention. Inconsistent managers debase their authority. Respect, trust, and authority are all gained by being consistent, and one single moment of inconsistency might ruin months of consistency and create motivational losses.

关键在于“始终如一”。并非大多数管理者不奖励达成目标的员工，他们确实会奖励。然而，他们往往缺乏一致性，导致达成目标的员工得不到应有的奖励。不幸的是，人们更容易记住那一次努力付诸东流的经历，而不是那九次获得奖励的经历。除非管理者能够始终如一地确保他承诺的后果（无论好坏）都能落实到位，否则他的话语将无法引起重视。缺乏一致性的管理者会损害自身的权威。尊重、信任和权威都源于始终如一，一次的不一致就可能毁掉数月的努力，并造成员工积极性的下降。

Many managers feel like they do not have the time and resources to be fully consistent in rewarding their employees. The next chapter, “Getting the time to do everything”, will address this issue.

许多管理者感觉自己没有足够的时间和资源来始终如一地奖励员工。下一章“如何挤出时间做所有事情”将探讨这个问题。

When facing an indifferent subordinate, the manager should teach him again that good outcomes follow good performance and that such good performance is attainable for him. The manager does not need to teach a demotivated subordinate to produce results; he needs to teach him that producing results brings good individual outcomes. These are two completely different concepts, and a manager focusing his efforts on the former while the bottleneck is the latter is setting himself up for frustration.

面对态度冷漠的下属，管理者应该再次强调，良好的表现会带来良好的结果，而良好的表现是可以实现的。管理者不需要教导一个缺乏动力的下属如何取得业绩，而是需要让他明白，取得业绩会带来良好的个人结果。这是两个截然不同的概念，如果管理者将精力集中在前者上，而忽略了后者，最终只会徒增挫败感。

(Of course, in case skills are the factor limiting the performance of the subordinate, and not motivation, then the manager will have to focus on ensuring he gets the required know-how.)

（当然，如果限制下属绩效的因素是技能而非积极性，那么经理就必须专注于确保下属获得所需的技能。）

Catch him right

抓住他

The way to teach the correct paradigm to your subordinates is by creating opportunities for them to learn that, if they fulfill their objectives, good things will happen to them and to their organization. This includes giving them small objectives and rewarding them for achieving them – mostly, with words of appreciation (as other kinds of rewards should be reserved for excellent performers).

向下属传授正确思维模式的方法是，创造机会让他们明白，如果他们完成目标，他们自身和组织都会受益。这包括给他们设定一些小目标，并在他们达成目标后给予奖励——主要是口头表扬（其他类型的奖励应该留给表现卓越的员工）。

The manager should only reward achieved objectives; he should not reward effort which did not achieve objectives nor saying nice words even if the “difficult employee” did not achieve the objective.

经理应该只奖励已经达成目标的员工；不应该奖励没有达成目标的努力，也不应该对没有达成目标的员工说好话，即使该员工没有达成目标。

If the difficult employee fails to achieve the objective (regardless of whether he tried and failed or failed to try), then the manager should give him a smaller objective. But the manager should never stop proposing smaller and smaller objectives with the hope of catching him achieving one and rewarding him for that.

如果难管的员工未能达成目标（无论他是尝试过但失败了，还是根本没尝试），那么经理应该给他设定一个更小的目标。但是，经理绝不能停止设定越来越小的目标，指望他能侥幸达成一个就奖励他。

There is an exception to the process of downsizing objectives until they are achieved – the risk that the difficult employee learns the wrong thing: that the less he does, the less he is asked. To prevent this, the process described above should always be accompanied by letting the employee know that his performance so far has been subpar and there are standards below which he will have to be let go, assuming that the local legislation allows it. If that is not possible, when he fails to reach an objective, do not lower the bar, instead increase the amount of time spent focusing on him. When he succeeds, do not raise the bar immediately – keep reinforcing the good behavior with words of appreciation for at least one or two weeks before raising the bar again.

在逐步降低目标直至达成的过程中，存在一个例外——那就是难管教的员工可能会误以为：做得越少，要求就越少。为了避免这种情况，上述流程应始终伴随着让员工知晓其目前的表现低于标准，并且存在必须达到的标准才能被解雇的情况（假设当地法律允许）。如果无法做到这一点，那么当他未能达成目标时，不要降低标准，而是增加对他的关注时间。当他取得成功时，不要立即提高标准——至少在一两周内持续给予表扬，以强化他的良好行为，然后再考虑提高标准。

To some, the process described above might seem utopian, but I assure you it works. If your experience tells you otherwise, it is because the process above wasn’t implemented consistently enough or clearly enough. An employee’s performance is always capped to the lowest between his internal drive and the consistency with which he has been taught to expect good outcomes in case of good performance and bad outcomes in case of bad performance.

对某些人来说，上述流程或许显得理想化，但我可以向你保证，它是行之有效的。如果你的经验与此相反，那是因为上述流程的执行不够连贯或不够清晰。员工的绩效始终处于其内在驱动力与他被灌输的预期结果一致性（即表现好就预期好，表现差就预期坏）之间的较低水平。

The Fourth Principle of Operational Excellence will discuss this concept more in depth.

卓越运营的第四项原则将更深入地探讨这一概念。

Rewards should always be of the appropriate size given the objective. The manager should not give an excessive reward, especially when compared to those given to employees who worked harder or better (otherwise those employees will soon learn that working sloppily is the more convenient choice). For this reason, the reward to small objectives should generally be some sincere words of praise and respect, such as “good job”; nothing more. If the objective, even though small, was indeed of help for the team, the manager should also remark this, with words such as “good job, this was helpful because…”.

奖励的数额应始终与目标相符。管理者不应给予过高的奖励，尤其不应与那些工作更努力或表现更出色的员工所获得的奖励相比（否则，这些员工很快就会认为偷工减料才是更轻松的选择）。因此，对于较小的目标，奖励通常只需一些真诚的赞扬和尊重，例如“干得好”，仅此而已。如果目标虽小，但确实对团队有所帮助，管理者也应该对此表示认可，例如“干得好，这很有帮助，因为……”。

If the manager manages to catch the “difficult employee” achieving an objective and rewards him in a fair way (not too much), then the employee will learn, at least partially, the link between fulfilling objectives and good outcomes happening. In some cases, catching him right once will be enough to start a virtuous circle of work ethic. In other cases, it will be necessary to catch him right a few times, perhaps even 10 or 20.

如果经理能够发现“难搞的员工”完成了目标，并给予公平的奖励（不要过度），那么这位员工至少会部分地理解完成目标与取得良好结果之间的联系。在某些情况下，一次正确的奖励就足以开启一种良性循环的工作态度。而在另一些情况下，则需要多次奖励，甚至可能需要十次或二十次。

As a manager, you should never reward effort; only results. Otherwise, you will end up with a team in whose members focus on signaling effort rather than bringing results.

作为管理者，你永远不应该奖励努力，而应该只奖励结果。否则，你的团队最终只会让成员们只关注如何展现自己的努力，而不是如何创造业绩。

Effort which isn’t conducive to the success of your organization should never be praised, not even with a “thank you”. It is respectful to acknowledge effort, though, with sentences such as “I noticed the effort you put, but you did not achieve the objective, and that is what ultimately matters.”

如果努力对组织的成功没有帮助，就不应该表扬，哪怕只是一句“谢谢”。但是，尊重地承认努力是可以的，比如可以说：“我注意到了你的努力，但你没有达到目标，而这才是最终重要的。”

Objectives should be human and sustainable – a topic discussed more in detail in the chapter on the First Principle of Operational Excellence.

目标应该以人为本且可持续——这一主题在关于卓越运营第一原则的章节中有更详细的讨论。

Sometimes, with difficult employees, it is effective to “carve a role” for them. Basketball fans can think of Dennis Rodman: a “bad boy” who excelled at a valuable yet ignored-by-others responsibility: rebounding. Find a skill or interest that the difficult employee has but others in the team lack. It might not be a skill required by the job description, but it has to be relevant to Operations. Then, try to assign to him some small objective related to it. Try to make him feel proud of his work ethic related to that skill or interest. Work ethic is contagious; it will spread to other aspects of his role.

有时候，对于难缠的员工，为他们“量身打造角色”会很有效。篮球迷们可以想想丹尼斯·罗德曼：一个“坏小子”，却在篮板这项重要但常被忽视的工作中表现出色。找到这位难缠的员工拥有而团队其他成员缺乏的技能或兴趣。这项技能或兴趣可能并非岗位职责所要求的，但必须与运营相关。然后，尝试给他分配一些与此相关的小目标。努力让他为自己运用这项技能或兴趣所展现出的职业道德感到自豪。职业道德具有感染力，它会渗透到他工作的其他方面。

To summarize:

总结起来：

1) Give the difficult employee objectives he can achieve.

1）给有挑战性的员工设定他能够实现的目标。

2) Catch him doing something right, such as fulfilling objectives or following rules.

2）发现他做对了事情，比如完成了目标或遵守了规则。

3) If he does so, thank or praise him appropriately, then raise the bar – but not too much.

3）如果他这样做，就适当地感谢或表扬他，然后提高标准——但不要太高。

4) If he does not, lower the bar and try again – but not too much.

4）如果他不听，降低标准再试一次——但不要降低太多。

Remember: one key part of Operational Excellence is to bring clarity and inevitability to the link between achieving objectives and individual outcomes.

记住：卓越运营的一个关键部分是明确实现目标与个人成果之间的联系，并使其具有必然性。

Motivational losses

动机损失

Every time an employee thinks he achieved an objective but does not get rewarded appropriately, he suffers a motivational loss.

每当一名员工认为自己实现了目标，但却没有得到适当的奖励时，他的积极性就会受到打击。

Some employees are more internally motivated and can withstand a few motivational losses without being affected in their day-to-day, but any employee has a “breaking point” where, after enough motivational losses, he will lose all enthusiasm and become a difficult employee or quit the company.

有些员工更有内在动力，能够承受一些动力上的打击而不会影响日常工作，但任何员工都有一个“崩溃点”，在经历足够多的动力打击后，他就会失去所有热情，变成一个难缠的员工，或者离开公司。

It is therefore extremely important that managers avoid any form of motivational loss in their subordinates, and this includes avoiding ambiguous objectives.

因此，管理者必须避免下属受到任何形式的激励打击，这其中就包括避免设定模糊的目标。

If the objective assigned to a subordinate is not clear, then it is possible that the subordinate equivocates and produces a work which he genuinely believes achieved the result he was tasked with. In this case, when the manager will have to tell him that his work was not good enough, the subordinate will suffer a great motivational loss: he expected a praise and received a reprimand instead.

如果分配给下属的目标不明确，那么下属可能会含糊其辞，并提交一份他真心认为已经达到任务要求的成果。在这种情况下，当经理不得不告诉他工作做得不够好时，下属的积极性会受到极大的打击：他原本期待的是表扬，结果却受到了批评。

Unambiguous objectives are necessary to avoid motivational losses (this concept will be the topic of the First Principle of Operational Excellence).

明确的目标是避免失去动力的必要条件（这一概念将是卓越运营第一原则的主题）。

Toxic employees

有毒的员工

The above notwithstanding, some employees are not just “difficult”. They are toxic. Whereas difficult employees just forgot (or never learned) the relationship between fulfilling objectives and good outcomes, toxic employees operate from a different set of beliefs and paradigms that are destructive to the Operational Culture of the team.

尽管如此，有些员工不仅仅是“难相处”，他们简直就是“毒瘤”。难相处的员工只是忘记了（或者从未学会）完成目标与取得良好结果之间的关系，而“毒瘤”员工则基于一套截然不同的信念和思维模式，这些信念和模式会破坏团队的运营文化。

Whereas difficult employees should be treated as potential assets and trained so that they become one, toxic ones should be treated as liabilities, and action should be taken to let them go, if allowed by the local legislation.

对于难缠的员工，应该将其视为潜在的资产并进行培训，使其成为资产；而对于有害的员工，则应该将其视为负债，如果当地法律允许，则应采取措施将其解雇。

In my experience, companies both overestimate the percentage of toxic employees (most are just difficult ones) and underestimate the need of letting them go as fast as possible, if allowed.

根据我的经验，公司既高估了有毒员工的比例（大多数只是难相处的员工），又低估了如果允许的话，尽快让他们离开的必要性。

Firing toxic employees might seem cruel, but keeping them in is more cruel: to their colleagues (whose efforts become devaluated), to the company (whose situation becomes harder, as it is burdened by the toxic employee) and to the employee itself (who could benefit for a change of environment or from a strong signal that his behavior has to change for good things to happen for him). Of course, firing should be a last recourse solution after having competently and wholeheartedly given him chances to change his behavior and support towards it, to validate the hypothesis that his toxicity is an inherent part of who he currently is and not a temporary reaction to an unconducive environment.

解雇有毒员工或许看似残酷，但留着他们则更加残酷：对他们的同事（他们的努力会被贬低）、对公司（公司会因为有毒员工的拖累而处境更加艰难）、对员工自身（他或许能从环境的改变中受益，或者从这强烈的信号中意识到，他的行为必须改变才能获得更好的发展）。当然，解雇应该是最后的手段，必须在充分且真诚地给予他改变行为的机会和支持之后，以验证他的毒性行为是否是其性格的固有组成部分，而非对不利环境的暂时反应。

Summary

概括

If you have difficult employees, you need to get them to experience the link between fulfilling objectives and good personal outcomes.

如果你的员工比较难管教，你需要让他们体会到完成目标与获得良好个人成果之间的联系。

1) Give them achievable objectives.

1）给他们设定可实现的目标。

2) Catch them doing something right, such as fulfilling objectives or following rules.

2）发现他们做对了事情，比如完成目标或遵守规则。

3) If they do so, thank or praise them appropriately, then raise the bar – but not too much.

3）如果他们这样做，要适当地感谢或表扬他们，然后提高标准——但不要太高。

4) If they do not, lower the bar and try again – but not too much.

4）如果他们不满意，降低标准再试一次——但不要降低太多。

# ↩

Getting the time to do everything

有时间做所有事

As a manager, you will most likely be haunted by days with too much to do and too little time.

作为一名管理者，你很可能会经常遇到事情太多、时间太少的情况。

For many managers, the reaction is working longer hours. This might be needed in case of exceptional deadlines, such as the last days of the year, but is never a good idea when its application is too frequent – more than 6-8 weeks per year. Chronic overtime brings stress and jadedness, both of which increase the risk of mistakes and limit the professional growth of the manager.

许多管理者应对这种情况的方式是延长工作时间。在遇到特殊截止日期时，例如年底最后几天，加班或许是必要的，但如果过于频繁——每年超过 6-8 周——就绝非明智之举。长期加班会带来压力和疲惫，这两者都会增加出错的风险，并限制管理者的职业发展。

Moreover, whereas in companies with poor Operational Excellence working overtime signals commitment, in companies with good Operational Excellence it signals structural problems such as the inability to prioritize effectively and get stuff done.

此外，在运营效率低下的公司里，加班表示敬业；而在运营效率高的公司里，加班则表明存在结构性问题，例如无法有效地确定优先事项和完成工作。

I once overheard an executive saying that he could not promote that employee who was working long hours because, if he did, the employee would find himself with too many responsibilities to juggle and would either have to increment his working hours to the point of a burnout, or inevitably “let some ball drop” and underperform. (Imagine the shock if the employee learnt that – he thought that working long hours would help his career!)

我曾无意中听到一位高管说，他不能提拔那位长时间工作的员工，因为如果提拔了，这位员工会发现自己要承担太多责任，要么不得不增加工作时间直至精疲力竭，要么不可避免地会“疏忽大意”，导致业绩下滑。（想象一下，如果这位员工知道这一点，该有多震惊——他原本以为长时间工作对他的职业发展有帮助！）

Let me be clear: it is not working overtime which is bad. In small doses, it is good. It is systematically working overtime which is bad. The former represents taking care of unusual spikes in workload, whereas the latter represents working overtime to take care of the usual workload – an indicator of a structural problem.

我要澄清一点：加班本身并不坏。少量加班是有益的。但长期持续加班才是坏事。前者是为了应对工作量突然激增的情况，而后者则是为了完成日常工作量而加班——这表明公司存在结构性问题。

Being understaffed might be the temporary reason for a chronically high workload, but it is never the long-term reason. A good organization which finds itself understaffed – due to the sudden leave of a few employees or due to a sudden increase in business – would quickly react and hire the missing talent. If it doesn’t, it might be for three reasons: the Top Management is not competent or committed enough, the business is horrible (your company operates in a shrinking or unprofitable market), or managers are not good at prioritizing. If one of the first two cases applies to your organization – consider changing company, to avoid fighting an uphill battle. If instead your case is the third one – bad prioritization – the rest of this chapter will be useful to you.

人手不足可能是工作量长期居高不下的暂时原因，但绝非长久之计。一个优秀的组织如果因为少数员工突然离职或业务激增而面临人手短缺，会迅速做出反应，招聘所需人才。如果组织没有这样做，可能有三个原因：高层管理人员能力不足或不够尽责；业务状况糟糕（公司身处萎缩或亏损的市场）；或者管理者不善于分清轻重缓急。如果前两种情况适用于您的组织，不妨考虑换一家公司，以免陷入困境。如果是第三种情况——优先级排序错误——那么本章的其余部分将对您有所帮助。

The source of problems

问题的根源

Each problem has a root cause. For example, your subordinates might continuously ask you for questions on a class of matters because the topic is not clear to them.

每个问题都有其根本原因。例如，你的下属可能会不断地就某一类问题向你提问，因为他们对这方面的内容并不理解。

If, when they ask you for advice, you answer their direct question without training them to answer by themselves, they will keep asking you the same questions all the time, causing you to spend too much time on it.

如果当他们向你寻求建议时，你直接回答他们的问题，而不训练他们自己回答，他们就会一直问你同样的问题，导致你花费太多时间。

In general, root causes keep generating problems. If you only solve problems without addressing their root cause, the root cause will keep throwing problems at you. Solving the root cause is the only action which will stop the flow of problems. Just like, in a sinking ship, throwing water overboard with a bucket will accomplish nothing at all if there is a hole from which the water keeps flowing in.

一般来说，问题的根源在于持续不断的根源性问题。如果你只解决问题而不解决根本原因，根源性问题就会不断地给你带来新的问题。只有解决根本原因才能真正阻止问题的持续发生。这就好比一艘正在下沉的船，如果船上有个洞，水不断从那里涌进来，那么用桶往外泼水也无济于事。

Every person with time problems has a prioritization problem. They only work on their superficial problems, on the urgent, waiting for the “perfect day” in which to address the root causes of their constant flow of problems. Sadly, that day will never come.

每个有时间问题的人都存在优先级排序问题。他们只处理表面问题和紧急事项，等待着“完美时机”来解决这些问题源源不断的根本原因。可悲的是，那一天永远不会到来。

The day their problems will end will be the day they decide to work on the root causes of their problems, despite the problems they are facing.

他们的问题最终会解决的那一天，就是他们下定决心解决问题的根本原因的那一天，尽管他们目前面临着各种问题。

Managing the urgent

应对紧急情况

Every day, there is something urgent to do. It is hard to find some time to work on the important – addressing root causes.

每天都有紧急的事情要做，很难抽出时间来处理真正重要的事情——解决根本原因。

However, the very important never looks urgent. Solving root causes will always appear less urgent than solving the problems they generated.

然而，真正重要的事情往往看起来并不紧迫。解决根本原因总是不如解决由此产生的问题那样紧迫。

Good managers aren’t fooled by urgency, and they know that their job is to work on the very important even when it doesn’t seem urgent, ignoring the urgent if they must.

优秀的管理者不会被紧迫感所迷惑，他们知道自己的工作是处理非常重要的事情，即使这些事情看起来并不紧急，如果必须的话，他们也可以忽略紧急的事情。

Companies with bad Operational Culture reward the managers who work on the urgent. Instead, companies with good Operational Culture reward those who work on the important. They do so by subordinating managers’ results on the urgent to their results on the important. This might seem counterintuitive, but for example, Toyota reportedly had a policy where a manager could not get a promotion unless, regardless of the personal results he achieved, he also completed some goals regarding the personal development of his subordinates (i.e., taking care of the root causes).

运营文化不良的公司会奖励那些只处理紧急事务的管理者。相反，运营文化良好的公司会奖励那些只处理重要事务的管理者。他们会将管理者在紧急事务上的业绩置于重要事务业绩之下。这看似有悖常理，但例如，据报道丰田公司曾有一项政策：管理者必须完成一些与下属个人发展相关的目标（即解决根本问题），才能获得晋升，而这与他个人的业绩无关。

This does not mean that the urgent cannot be important. It means that what to work on should be chosen solely on the basis of importance, disregarding urgency.

这并不意味着紧急的事情就不重要。而是说，选择工作内容应该完全基于重要性，而忽略紧急程度。

Policies and tools conducive to addressing root causes will be discussed in later chapters of this book; for the moment, the reader is invited to just focus on the following principle: the only way to solve your problems is indirectly by addressing their root causes; solving the problems directly will instead generate more problems.

本书后续章节将讨论有助于解决根本原因的政策和工具；目前，请读者只需关注以下原则：解决问题的唯一方法是通过间接解决其根本原因；直接解决问题反而会产生更多问题。

Getting more time

获得更多时间

It is possible that, to your eyes, each of your subordinates is a source of problems to solve. If you only work on the problems they bring to your attention, they will keep bringing new problems to your attention, with your availability as the only limit.

或许在你眼里，每个下属都是需要解决的问题。如果你只处理他们提出的问题，他们就会不断地提出新的问题，而你是否有空就是唯一的限制。

I can guarantee that, if you spend more time today to train them to solve their own problems by themselves, tomorrow you will have much more time available, as they will not be depending on you anymore.

我可以保证，如果你今天多花些时间训练他们自己解决问题，明天你就会有更多的时间，因为他们不再依赖你了。

Instead, if today you are answering their questions waiting for the day they do not have questions to train them to solve their problems by themselves, know that day will never come.

相反，如果你今天还在回答他们的问题，等待着他们不再有问题的那一天来训练他们自己解决问题，那么你要知道，那一天永远不会到来。

Of course, today you won’t have the time to train all your subordinates on all matters – probably, you won’t even have the time to train a single employee on all his matters. However, you have the time to train one of your subordinates to solve one type of problems he might be raising to your attention. If you do that, tomorrow you will have a bit more time (because that subordinate will not be generate any more problems of that kind). You can use the time you saved to train a second subordinate on another class of problems, saving you more time during the following days. If you keep doing that, day after day, after a few months you’ll soon find yourself with much more time at your disposal.

当然，今天你不可能有时间培训所有下属的所有技能——或许你甚至没有时间培训任何一个员工的所有技能。但是，你可以培训一位下属解决他可能提出的某一类问题。如果你这样做，明天你就会有更多的时间（因为这位下属不会再提出这类问题）。你可以利用节省下来的时间培训另一位下属解决另一类问题，从而在接下来的几天里节省更多时间。如果你每天都这样做，几个月后，你就会发现自己拥有了更多的时间。

If your subordinates come too often to you with questions regarding the same topic which require context-based answers, consider having a subject matter expert. He is a senior employee knowledgeable on the matter who would be responsible for answering questions on that topic – freeing time for yourself to do your job.

如果你的下属频繁就同一主题向你提问，而这些提问又需要结合具体情况才能解答，那么不妨考虑聘请一位该领域的专家。这位专家通常是资深员工，对相关领域非常了解，他将负责解答这些问题，从而让你腾出时间专注于自己的工作。

Let me debunk a myth here: having someone else do tasks which are not part of your job description is not laziness. It is lazy to do them yourself because you do not want to do the emotional work of putting yourself in the conditions of doing the tasks which are critical for your role.

让我来澄清一个误区：让别人做那些不属于你工作职责范围的任务并非懒惰。真正懒惰的是自己去做这些事，因为你不想付出情感上的努力，不想让自己置身于完成那些对你的工作至关重要的任务的情境中。

The same might apply to other problems you might have, coming from sources other than your subordinates. Perhaps, your customers, your boss, your peers, bureaucracy, and so on… For each problem that you repeatedly encounter in your life, acknowledge that there is a root cause that keeps throwing new instances of that problem to you; then, work on solving that root cause ignoring the problems it is throwing at you. That’s the only way to avoid having to face the same problems in the future.

同样的道理也适用于你可能遇到的其他问题，这些问题可能并非来自你的下属。例如，你的客户、你的老板、你的同事、官僚机构等等……对于生活中反复出现的每一个问题，都要认识到其根源在于某个原因，正是这个原因不断引发新的问题；然后，着手解决这个根源，而忽略它所带来的其他问题。这是避免将来再次面对同样问题的唯一途径。

Chronic problems are life’s way to tell you to do something you didn’t do yet.

慢性问题是生活的一种方式，它提醒你去做一些你还没有做过的事情。

A good question

问得好

If you keep spending your workdays like you’ve been doing recently, how will the Operational Culture of your team look like in a couple of years?

如果你继续像最近这样度过你的工作日，几年后你的团队运营文化会变成什么样子？

How will your work life look like?

你的工作生活会是什么样子？

An introduction

引言

The content above is just an introduction to the topic of personal productivity and on the actions you should be taking as a manager. You will find more practical content in the core of this book.

以上内容仅是对个人效率以及作为管理者应采取的行动的简要介绍。本书的核心内容将包含更多实用技巧。

Action point

行动要点

Make a list of recurring problems which are consuming your time and select the one which is consuming the most. Is there any action you can take today to reduce future wastes of time originating from that problem? Can you address its root cause?

列出所有反复出现且耗费你时间的问题，并从中选出耗时最长的问题。你今天可以采取哪些措施来减少未来因该问题造成的时间浪费？你能找到问题的根本原因并解决它吗？

# ↩

Creating trust

建立信任

As a manager, you want to have the trust of your subordinates. They will share more information with you, they will escalate problems sooner when needed – allowing you to tackle them before they become too big – and they will work on the objectives you assign them faster and better, without questioning them.

作为管理者，你需要赢得下属的信任。他们会与你分享更多信息，在必要时更早地上报问题——让你能够在问题变得棘手之前解决它们——并且他们会更快更好地完成你分配的目标，而不会提出质疑。

However, trust is not a given; it must be earned. Below are some requirements for trust and how to achieve them.

然而，信任并非与生俱来，而是需要努力赢得的。以下是建立信任的一些必要条件以及如何获得这些条件。

Competence : your subordinates will not trust your decisions if they do not believe you are competent at your job. Three factors will influence the perception of your competence: your background (have you been working in the field for long enough? Do you have previous experience in Operations?), your achievements (did you achieve great results in the past? Did the teams you manage achieve great results?), and whether you listen to your subordinates and explain your decisions to them.

能力：如果你的下属不相信你胜任工作，他们就不会信任你的决定。有三个因素会影响别人对你能力的感知：你的背景（你在这个领域工作的时间够长吗？你之前有过运营方面的经验吗？）、你的成就（你过去是否取得过优异的成绩？你管理的团队是否取得了优异的成绩？），以及你是否倾听下属的意见并向他们解释你的决定。

You might have limited influence today on the first two points – background and achievements – but you can work on the third one. As a manager, you have a privileged point of view of the business, having access to much broader information than your subordinates. Therefore, you might “know better”. However, if you take decisions without listening to your subordinates nor explaining to them the reasons for which you took such decisions, they might not trust that you do indeed “know better”.

今天，你或许对前两点——背景和成就——的影响力有限，但你可以着手处理第三点。作为一名管理者，你拥有独特的视角，能够获取比下属更广泛的信息。因此，你或许“更了解情况”。然而，如果你在做决定时既不听取下属的意见，也不向他们解释决策原因，他们可能就不会相信你真的“更了解情况”。

Often, your subordinates will not agree on your decisions. However, if you gave them reasons to believe you genuinely listened to their full point of view, even if you end up taking a decision they disagree with, they will not resent you for it – at least not in the long term. Instead, if they are on the impression that you did not listen to them fully – regardless of whether you actually did – taking a decision they do not agree with will be perceived as incompetence and cause a break of trust.

很多时候，你的下属不会同意你的决定。但是，如果你让他们相信你真正倾听了他们的观点，即使你最终做出了他们不认同的决定，他们也不会因此怨恨你——至少从长远来看不会。相反，如果他们觉得你没有认真听取他们的意见——无论你是否真的听取了——那么你做出的他们不认同的决定就会被视为无能，并导致信任破裂。

In later chapters of this book, I will describe a few Best Practices which are designed to ensure that your subordinates feel listened to and trust your decisions.

在本书的后续章节中，我将介绍一些最佳实践，旨在确保你的下属感到你的意见被倾听，并信任你的决定。

Visibility: your subordinates will not trust your decisions if they do not believe you are at least somehow knowledgeable about their job. This requires you to spend at least part of your time at your subordinate’s floor, at their desks, with their teams. If you only meet them in your office or in conference rooms, they will have the impression that you do not really know what’s going on in their work life – regardless of whether this is actually the case.

可见性：如果你的下属认为你对他们的工作缺乏了解，他们就不会信任你的决定。这就要求你至少花一些时间在下属所在的楼层、他们的办公桌旁，与他们的团队一起工作。如果你只在办公室或会议室与他们见面，他们会觉得你并不真正了解他们的工作情况——无论事实是否如此。

In a later chapter of this book, I will describe a Best Practice, “Management Walks”, which is designed to address this point.

在本书的后续章节中，我将介绍一种最佳实践“管理巡视”，旨在解决这个问题。

Fairness: as a manager, you should strive to enforce rules and evaluate people in a fair way which is predictable and identical for all. No favorites, no exceptions, no “judging the effort” or “excusing the circumstances”. Judging everyone equally will prevent them from thinking that your decisions are personal. If, instead, you use double standards or subjective judgements, your subordinates will have the possibility to think you are making it personal and they will trust you less.

公平：作为管理者，你应该努力执行规则，并以公平、可预测且对所有人都相同的方式评估员工。不偏袒任何人，不搞特殊，不“看重努力程度”或“为特殊情况开脱”。平等对待每个人可以避免他们觉得你的决定带有个人偏见。相反，如果你采用双重标准或主观判断，你的下属可能会认为你是在针对他们个人，从而降低对你的信任。

Principled: counterintuitively, people cannot fully trust someone who is loyal to individuals. What if he will have to decide between two people he swore loyalty to? People only trust those whose behavior they can predict [4] , and the behavior of those who are loyal to individuals is fickle. Instead, people who are loyal to principles are fully predictable and therefore can be fully trusted.

原则至上：与直觉相反，人们无法完全信任一个忠于个人的人。如果他必须在两个他曾宣誓效忠的人之间做出选择呢？人们只信任那些行为可预测的人[4]，而忠于个人的人的行为反复无常。相反，忠于原则的人的行为完全可预测，因此可以完全信任。

If you consistently act and objectively evaluate people based on fair principles which are conspicuously known and do not change over time (so, no surprises nor lunaticity), your subordinates will be able to fully trust you. They will be able to predict how you will react to their actions. They will know that, if they come to you confessing a good faith mistake, you will not think less of them and will react appropriately. They will be more open with you and, eventually, will begin acting according to your principles too.

如果你始终如一地秉持公正客观的原则行事，并根据这些原则客观地评价他人，而且这些原则要广为人知且不会随时间改变（也就是说，不会出现任何意外或荒谬的情况），你的下属就能完全信任你。他们能够预测你会如何回应他们的行为。他们会知道，如果他们出于善意坦白错误，你不会因此而轻视他们，而是会给予恰当的回应。他们会更加坦诚地与你交流，最终也会开始按照你的原则行事。

Do not water down your authority

不要削弱你的权威

Bad managers think that their authority derives from their title. This is obviously not descriptive of reality; using job titles as coercion only brings minimum performance and only while the boss is looking.

糟糕的管理者认为他们的权威来源于头衔。这显然不符合现实；以职位头衔作为胁迫手段，只能带来最低限度的绩效，而且只有在老板在场时才会奏效。

Good managers know that their authority derives from their consistency in keeping their word, especially about the consequences of having fulfilled individual objectives or having failed to do so.

优秀的管理者知道，他们的权威来源于他们始终信守承诺，尤其是在实现或未能实现个人目标所带来的后果方面。

A respected manager is a manager whose objectives lead to good things when they are completed (for the employee, for the team and for the company) and to bad things when they are not.

受人尊敬的经理，其目标实现时会带来好的结果（对员工、团队和公司而言），而目标未能实现时则会带来坏的结果。

Some examples of behaviors which water down the authority of the manager:

以下是一些削弱管理者权威的行为示例：

  • Failing to appropriately acknowledge those who fulfill their objectives.
    未能对那些实现目标的人给予应有的认可。
  • Setting objectives which, when completed, do not brings value to anyone (for example, asking to prepare a report which no one will read).
    设定一些目标，完成之后不会给任何人带来价值（例如，要求准备一份没有人会阅读的报告）。
  • Asking to do something which, if not done, does not bring any negative consequences (for example, asking everyone to wear their safety helmets and then not caring whether the employees actually do it).
    要求做某事，即使不做也不会带来任何负面后果（例如，要求每个人都戴上安全帽，然后不在乎员工是否真的戴上了）。

Some examples of behaviors which build authority:

以下是一些有助于建立权威的行为示例：

  • Setting an objective and acknowledging the result, rewarding or reprimanding the employee proportionally.
    设定目标并认可结果，按比例奖励或惩罚员工。
  • Setting objectives which, if completed, bring a tangible positive improvement to the team or to the organization. (“It was really important to work on.”)
    设定目标，如果完成这些目标，就能为团队或组织带来切实的积极改进。（“这项工作真的非常重要。”）
  • Never failing to follow-up on one’s word (“Yesterday I asked you to send me that report. You didn’t send it yet. That’s not good, because now I cannot use it for tomorrow’s decision. When I ask something, it is because it’s important.”).
    从不食言（“昨天我让你把那份报告发给我。你还没发。这不好，因为我明天就没法用它做决定了。我提要求，都是因为这件事很重要。”）。
  • Judging fairly (this gives authority to both the person doing it – the manager – and to the principles using for judging).
    公正地评判（这赋予了评判者——经理——以及评判所依据的原则以权威）。

Authority is trust that one’s word is consequential, and that is mainly a function of consistency.

权威是人们相信一个人的话有分量，而这主要取决于言行一致。

# ↩

Part 1:
The Four Principles of Operational Excellence

第一部分：卓越运营的四大原则

# ↩

The 1 st Principle
of Operational Excellence:

Good managers set unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives

卓越运营的第一原则：优秀的管理者会设定明确、具体且可奖励的目标。

The most important task of a manager is performance management: setting objectives for his subordinates and holding them accountable for their results. Performance management impacts both the short-term performance of the team (directing and motivating the subordinates on their current tasks) and its long-term performance (powerfully communicating values and standards by rewarding desired behaviors and punishing undesired ones).

管理者最重要的任务是绩效管理：为下属设定目标并让他们对结果负责。绩效管理既影响团队的短期绩效（指导和激励下属完成当前任务），也影响团队的长期绩效（通过奖励期望的行为和惩罚不期望的行为，有效地传达价值观和标准）。

When a manager fails to execute on performance management, he compromises the good results he might have obtained in other areas , such as communication, hiring and decision making. Skillful managers will still find themselves with an underperforming team, if they did not demonstrate to them that individual outcomes consistently follow individual performance on the objectives they have been given and on living the Core Values of the company.

当一位管理者未能有效执行绩效管理时，他就会损害在其他领域（例如沟通、招聘和决策）可能取得的良好成果。即使是经验丰富的管理者，如果他们没有向团队成员证明个人绩效与既定目标以及对公司核心价值观的践行密切相关，最终也会面临团队绩效不佳的困境。

Many managers have trouble with consistently holding their subordinates accountable in a fair and constructive way. Some are uncomfortable with telling their underperforming subordinates that they did a bad job, especially when it could be argued that “they did what they could”. Others fail to consistently reward the good performance of their employees, because they lack the budget or time to do so. And some fail to be fair in their evaluations, because they were not clear in how performance was to be evaluated or because they considered factors other than performance.

许多管理者在公平、建设性地追究下属责任方面存在困难。有些管理者不愿直接指出表现不佳的下属的错误，尤其是在对方可能辩解说“他们已经尽力了”的情况下。另一些管理者则因为缺乏预算或时间，无法持续奖励员工的优秀表现。还有一些管理者在绩效评估中不够公平，原因可能是他们没有明确绩效评估的标准，或者考虑了绩效以外的其他因素。

There is one common trait shared by managers who have trouble with consistently holding their subordinates accountable: they do not set clear objectives. This is the cause of most of their problems with regards to performance management.

那些在绩效管理方面难以有效追究下属责任的管理者，都有一个共同的特点：他们没有设定清晰的目标。这正是他们绩效管理中大部分问题的根源所在。

The 2 problems of setting ambiguous objectives

设定模糊目标的两个问题

Managers who set ambiguous objectives have two problems. First, a performance problem. The more ambiguous an objective, the higher the chances that a worker misinterprets it and fails to fulfill it. Moreover, the more ambiguous an objective, the more wiggling room subordinates have to interpret the orders of the manager in a way that allows them to avoid doing the tasks they are uncomfortable with, ultimately affecting the end result.

设定模糊目标的管理者会面临两个问题。首先是绩效问题。目标越模糊，员工误解目标、无法完成目标的可能性就越高。此外，目标越模糊，下属就越有回旋余地去解读管理者的指令，从而逃避他们不愿做的任务，最终影响最终结果。

Second, the lack of clarity makes it challenging for managers to hold their subordinates accountable. The more ambiguous the objective, the more a subordinate who failed to achieve it can argue he actually did what was requested and therefore should not be hold accountable. This makes it harder for the manager to follow through with the appropriate consequences, such as negative feedback, reprimands or disciplinary actions. The consequences of a lack of clarity are negative even in the case in which the manager does follow up with consequences, as the subordinate may end up frustrated and lose motivation; moreover, there is a chance that he might if he thinks he has been unfairly judged.

其次，目标不明确使得管理者难以追究下属的责任。目标越模糊，未能达成目标的下属就越有可能辩称自己已经完成了任务，因此不应承担责任。这使得管理者难以落实适当的后果，例如负面反馈、训诫或纪律处分。即使管理者最终采取了相应的措施，目标不明确带来的后果依然是负面的，因为下属可能会感到沮丧并失去动力；此外，如果下属认为自己受到了不公平的评价，也可能会更加消极。

Because of the two phenomena described above, managers who set ambiguous objectives tend to have underperforming subordinates and are less likely to hold them accountable for their underperformance.

由于上述两种现象，设定模糊目标的管理者往往会有表现不佳的下属，并且不太可能追究他们的责任。

The vicious circle of loose performance management

绩效管理松散的恶性循环

Failing to consistently apply individual outcomes to the performance of subordinates further exacerbates the problem. Once a manager has let someone off the hook, he sets a precedent for others, making it easier for them to argue that they should also be given a pass. This makes it even more difficult in the future for the manager to be consistent in the application of consequences and further deteriorates the Operational Culture of the team.

未能始终如一地将个人绩效考核结果应用于下属表现，会进一步加剧问题。一旦管理者放过某人，就为其他人树立了先例，使他们更容易为自己辩解，认为自己也应该得到宽恕。这使得管理者在未来更难始终如一地执行绩效考核，并进一步恶化团队的运营文化。

Good managers are aware of this vicious circle. They prevent it by setting clear objectives and by being fully consistent in applying consequences. As a result, their workers know what is expected of them and the managers themselves can be comfortable doing their job of performance management later.

优秀的管理者深知这种恶性循环。他们通过设定清晰的目标并始终如一地执行相应的惩罚措施来避免这种情况的发生。因此，员工清楚自己的职责所在，管理者也能更安心地开展后续的绩效管理工作。

Bad managers describe objectives that can be understood. Good managers describe objectives which cannot be misinterpreted.

糟糕的管理者描述的目标容易被理解，而优秀的管理者描述的目标则不会被误解。

# ↩


The 3 attributes of good objectives

好目标的三个特征

Good managers set objectives with 3 attributes:

优秀的管理者在设定目标时应具备以下三个特点：

Attribute

属性

Description

描述

Unambiguous

明确的

Good managers set unambiguous objectives by painting a visual description of what success looks like and asking their subordinates to repeat their understanding with their own words. This ensures that there is no way the employee can misunderstand the objective or later argue it wasn’t clear.

优秀的管理者会设定明确的目标，他们会用图像描述成功的样子，并要求下属用自己的语言复述他们的理解。这样就能确保员工不会误解目标，也不会事后质疑目标的清晰性。

Individual

个人

Good managers restrict the objective to something that the subordinate can impact with his individual contribution. This ensures that an employee cannot use his team’s lack of performance to cover or excuse his own underperformance.

优秀的管理者会将目标限定在下属能够通过个人贡献产生影响的范围内。这样就能确保员工无法利用团队业绩不佳来掩盖或开脱自身业绩不佳的借口。

Rewardable

可获得奖励

Good managers set ambitious yet achievable objectives.

优秀的管理者会设定既有挑战性又可实现的目标。

If the objective is not ambitious enough, the manager could find himself in the situation in which all his subordinates fulfilled their own objectives and yet, doing so did not generate enough value for the company to justify rewarding them with raises or promotions. This leads to hard-working employees getting frustrated with the lack of rewards and ending up either demotivated or quitting their job.

如果目标不够远大，管理者可能会遇到这样的情况：所有下属都完成了各自的目标，但公司却没有从中创造足够的价值，不足以给予他们加薪或晋升。这会导致勤奋的员工因缺乏奖励而感到沮丧，最终要么失去动力，要么选择离职。

Instead, good managers set objectives which are ambitious enough so that, in case of success, the company makes enough profit to reward the subordinate with part of the windfall.

相反，优秀的管理者会设定足够远大的目标，这样，如果目标成功，公司就能获得足够的利润，从而将部分意外之财奖励给下属。

Objectives also must be realistic. If the objective feels unattainable, most subordinates will act as if the potential reward is not even there. A few will instead overwork themselves to the point of suffering a burnout – an equally undesirable outcome.

目标也必须切合实际。如果目标感觉遥不可及，大多数下属会视而不见，仿佛潜在的回报根本不存在。少数人甚至会过度劳累，最终导致精疲力竭——这同样是不可取的后果。

Most managers understand the importance of the points above, but fail to consistently apply them in practice, for 6 reasons:

大多数管理者都明白以上几点的重要性，但却未能始终如一地在实践中加以运用，原因有六：

Objective is…

目标是……

Cause

原因

Explanation

解释

Ambiguous

模糊的

The manager is incompetent.

这位经理能力不足。

The manager does not know how to set clear objectives or why it is important to do so.

这位经理不知道如何设定明确的目标，也不知道为什么这样做很重要。

Ambiguous

模糊的

The manager wants to retain political power.

这位经理想要保住政治权力。

The blurrier the objectives, the more the manager can be subjective in his rewarding and thus draw power from his ability to apply such subjectivity.

目标越模糊，管理者在奖励时就越可以主观，从而通过运用这种主观性来获得权力。

Ambiguous

模糊的

The manager is afraid that he won’t be able to follow-up with rewards or punishments.

经理担心他无法对奖励或惩罚措施进行后续跟进。

The blurrier the objectives, the easier for the manager to confabulate a reason for which consequences should not follow results or lack thereof.

目标越模糊，管理者就越容易编造理由，让结果或缺乏结果不承担后果。

Ambiguous

模糊的

The manager is afraid that the team will not be able to produce satisfying results anyway.

经理担心球队无论如何都无法取得令人满意的成绩。

The blurrier the objectives, the easier for the manager to justify to his boss why his team underperformed but neither him nor individual members should be hold accountable.

目标越模糊，经理就越容易向上司解释为什么他的团队表现不佳，而他本人和团队成员都不应该承担责任。

Collective

集体

The manager dreads having any difficult conversation with individual subordinates.

经理害怕与个别下属进行任何棘手的谈话。

The manager assigns responsibilities to groups only, so that individual responsibility is unclear and cannot be rewarded nor punished. This does not mean that good managers do not use group objectives but that doing so is not sufficient; it is necessary to also use individual ones.

管理者只给团队分配职责，这样个人责任就不明确，也无法进行奖惩。这并非意味着优秀的管理者不使用团队目标，而是说仅仅使用团队目标是不够的；还需要设定个人目标。

Unrewardable

无益

The manager does not respect the capacities of his subordinates or his own ones and ends up assigning too conservative objectives.

这位经理既不尊重下属的能力，也不尊重自己的能力，最终设定了过于保守的目标。

Objectives should not be set so that they are comfortable, but so that good things happen if they are achieved.

设定目标不应该是为了让人感到舒适，而是为了在目标实现后带来好的结果。

In all but one of the rows above, when managers fail to set clear objectives it is not because of a lack of skills. Rather, it is because of some mental patterns of theirs that makes them believe that setting unclear objectives is the optimal choice.

在上述所有案例中，除了其中一行之外，管理者未能设定清晰目标并非因为缺乏技能，而是因为某些固有的思维模式让他们误以为设定模糊的目标才是最佳选择。

One particular instance of this phenomenon is the vicious circle of bad management, described below.

这种现象的一个典型例子是管理不善造成的恶性循环，如下所述。

Thriving in a dysfunctional culture

在功能失调的文化中蓬勃发展

Often, managers find themselves immersed in a dysfunctional culture where clarity and consistency are missing. Many react with coping behaviors such as joining others in setting unclear objectives and letting underperformance go unpunished. Their reaction to a lack of clarity and consistency is to behave with a similar lack of clarity and consistency themselves.

管理者常常发现自己身处一个功能失调的企业文化中，缺乏清晰度和一致性。许多人会采取一些应对措施，例如与他人一起设定模糊不清的目标，并对绩效不佳的情况不予惩罚。他们应对这种缺乏清晰度和一致性的方式，就是让自己也表现得同样缺乏清晰度和一致性。

However, by trying to fit in, they dug themselves a hole which only grows deeper. Because they set unclear and unambitious objectives, they cannot reward those employees who performed and cannot punish those who didn’t. Consequently, their team underperforms and, because it underperformed, the manager loses confidence in his capacities and in his team’s. Next time, he will set even more ambiguous, more collective and less rewardable goals. This is a vicious circle which happens whenever managers act reactively.

然而，他们为了迎合他人而挖了个坑，而且这个坑越挖越深。由于他们设定的目标模糊不清且缺乏挑战性，既无法奖励表现出色的员工，也无法惩罚表现不佳的员工。结果，他们的团队表现不佳，而团队表现不佳又导致经理对自己和团队的能力失去信心。下次，他会设定更加模糊、更具集体性且更难以实现的目标。每当管理者被动应对时，就会陷入这种恶性循环。

Whereas bad managers are reactive and focus on coping, good managers are proactive and fight to create an environment worth working in. Even when immersed in a culture where clarity and consistency are missing, they do the work of setting unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives. They know that this will make their follow-up job of performance management much easier and will break the vicious circle.

糟糕的管理者被动应对，只顾应付，而优秀的管理者则积极主动，努力营造一个值得投入的工作环境。即使身处缺乏清晰度和一致性的企业文化中，他们也会努力设定明确、个性化且可奖励的目标。他们深知，这样做会大大简化后续的绩效管理工作，并打破恶性循环。

Good managers do not wait for the perfect environment to do their work; rather, they realize that it is their job to create a conducive environment.

优秀的管理者不会等待完美的环境来开展工作；相反，他们意识到创造一个有利的环境是他们的职责。

Guilt and shame

内疚和羞耻

Guilt and shame by a manager are symptoms of insufficient clarity, individuality or ambitiousness during delegation. The higher the possibility that the subordinate might think he has done a good job when he actually didn’t, the more a manager feels uncomfortable in holding him accountable. If the manager had been perfectly clear while setting objectives, none of this would have happened.

管理者感到内疚和羞愧，往往是授权过程中缺乏清晰的思路、个性化的表达或不够积极主动的表现。下属越有可能误以为自己做得很好，而实际上并非如此，管理者就越难以追究其责任。如果管理者在设定目标时就做到了清晰明确，这一切就不会发生。

Good managers understand that each time they feel guilt or shame, it is because they have not been doing properly their work of setting unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives.

优秀的管理者明白，每当他们感到内疚或羞愧时，都是因为他们没有做好设定明确、个性化和可奖励目标的工作。

Good managers use these feelings as a signal that it is time to have an individual discussion with their subordinate, acknowledging that the previous objectives had not been set clearly, and setting new ones with the 3 attributes listed above.

优秀的管理者会利用这些感受作为信号，表明是时候与下属进行单独谈话了，承认之前的目标没有明确设定，并根据上面列出的 3 个特征设定新的目标。

Bad managers react to guilt and shame with avoidance; good ones use them as a signal that they should bring more clarity into objective-setting.

糟糕的管理者会逃避内疚和羞耻感；优秀的管理者则会将其视为一个信号，表明他们应该在目标设定方面更加明确。

Management is an incredibly simple job, in the absence of shame. Clarity is what prevents the shame from becoming part of the equation.

如果没有羞耻感，管理工作就非常简单。清晰的沟通是避免羞耻感介入的关键。

Lack of motivation

缺乏动力

When good managers spot a lack of motivation in their subordinates, they interpret it as a signal of a lack of clarity. Such lack of clarity might be of 3 kinds:

优秀的管理者一旦发现下属缺乏积极性，就会将其解读为缺乏清晰目标的信号。这种缺乏清晰目标的情况可能体现在以下三个方面：

- Lack of clarity of objectives: because the objectives are not clear, the subordinate is confused about what has to be done next. This undecidedness is often mistaken as a lack of motivation.

目标不明确：由于目标不明确，下属对下一步该做什么感到困惑。这种犹豫不决常常被误认为是缺乏动力。

- Lack of clarity of personal impact: because the objectives are not individual, the subordinate is unsure about the scope and importance of his personal impact and is less motivated towards taking effective action. Maybe, he waits for someone else in the team to take action. Or perhaps, he doesn’t want to risk overstepping on someone else. Either way, he doesn’t act proactively nor wholeheartedly.

- 个人影响不明确：由于目标并非针对个人，下属不确定自身影响的范围和重要性，因此缺乏采取有效行动的动力。他或许会等待团队中的其他人采取行动，又或许不想冒着得罪他人的风险。无论如何，他都无法积极主动、全心全意地投入工作。

- Lack of clarity of individual outcomes: because the objectives are not linked to clear individual outcomes dependent upon individual performance, the subordinate is not motivated to act outside of his comfort zone.

- 个人结果不明确：由于目标与取决于个人表现的明确个人结果没有联系，下属没有动力走出舒适区。

Good performance management empowers subordinates

良好的绩效管理能够赋予下属权力。

Managers who are relentless in applying the appropriate consequences to the performance of their subordinates are not selfish. On the contrary, good managers know that doing so is beneficial to the subordinates themselves. In companies where consistent performance management is missing, workers underperform. As a result, in the best case, their manager cannot show enough success to his superiors to justify getting the budget to offer bonuses, raises or promotions to his team. In the worst case, he has to lay off some of its members. Neither outcome is good for the subordinates.

对下属绩效毫不妥协、严格执行相应惩罚措施的管理者并非自私。相反，优秀的管理者深知这样做对下属自身有益。在缺乏持续绩效管理的公司里，员工绩效低下。结果，最好的情况是，管理者无法向上级证明足够的业绩，从而无法获得预算来为团队成员提供奖金、加薪或晋升。最糟糕的情况是，管理者不得不裁员。这两种结果对下属都不利。

Moreover, good managers know that good performance management is a great way to help their subordinates to realize their potential. Often, a subordinate has to get out of his comfort zone to do what it takes to fulfill an objective. Unless he is exceptionally proactive and internally motivated, he will need external incentives in order to do so. His manager is responsible for providing him with them, in the form of a trustworthy promise of good individual outcomes if he completes his objectives and of bad individual outcomes if he doesn’t.

此外，优秀的管理者深知，良好的绩效管理是帮助下属发挥潜能的有效途径。通常，下属需要走出舒适区才能完成目标。除非他非常积极主动且具有内在动力，否则他需要外部激励才能做到这一点。他的管理者有责任提供这种激励，具体表现为：如果他完成目标，将获得丰厚的个人奖励；如果他未能完成目标，则将面临相应的惩罚。

Good managers know that every employee benefits from reaching his potential. This leads to higher job satisfaction, higher self-respect, higher salary and higher job security. Therefore, they know that it is helpful and generous to set clear and ambitious objectives and to guarantee fair consequences. Conversely, it is those managers that are ambiguous in the definition of objectives and inconsistent in the application of consequences that are selfish. In order to feel more comfortable with themselves, they prioritize their own emotional comfort over the personal development of their subordinates.

优秀的管理者深知，充分发挥员工潜能对每位员工都有益。这能带来更高的工作满意度、更强的自尊心、更高的薪酬和更稳定的工作保障。因此，他们明白设定清晰且富有挑战性的目标，并保证公平的奖励，既有益又慷慨。相反，那些目标定义含糊不清、奖励执行前后矛盾的管理者才是自私的。为了让自己感觉更舒服，他们优先考虑自身的情感舒适，而非下属的个人发展。

Good performance management is human

良好的绩效管理是人为的。

Some managers are extremely consistent in their performance management but set excessively ambitious objectives. This might get a sudden increase in productivity in the short term, but always leads to disastrous performance over the long term, as employees are forced to throw the towel. This happens in two ways: some employees will feel like the objectives are unreachable or not worth the effort, whereas others will overwork themselves to the point of suffering a nervous breakdown. The consequence is the same: a team devoid of energy.

有些管理者在绩效管理方面非常严谨，但却设定了过高的目标。这或许能在短期内迅速提升生产力，但从长远来看，最终必然导致灾难性的绩效，因为员工会被迫放弃。这种情况主要有两种表现形式：一些员工会觉得目标遥不可及或不值得付出努力，而另一些员工则会过度劳累，最终导致精神崩溃。结果都是一样的：团队士气低落。

Good managers know that objectives must be ambitious yet human.

优秀的管理者明白，目标必须具有挑战性，但也要人性化。

Sometimes, good managers might require a performance burst from their subordinates – for example, in case of a rush order from one of their best customers. In that case, they might set a very ambitious objective. However, they make sure of two things: first, the higher-than-usual burst of work has to be appropriately rewarded (a celebration, paid time off, a bonus, opportunities for personal development, etc.); second, this cannot become business as usual. Requiring overtime a few weeks per year is a sign of a healthy company which can absorb temporary spikes in demand; chronically requiring overtime (whether formally or informally) is a sign of a dysfunctional company which tries to compensate its structural problems by burdening its employees.

有时，优秀的管理者可能会要求下属全力以赴，例如，当重要客户紧急下单时。在这种情况下，他们可能会设定一个非常高的目标。然而，他们会确保两件事：首先，这种超负荷的工作必须得到相应的奖励（例如庆祝活动、带薪休假、奖金、个人发展机会等）；其次，这种情况不能成为常态。每年要求员工加班几周，说明公司运营健康，能够应对暂时的需求高峰；而长期要求员工加班（无论正式还是非正式），则表明公司运转失灵，试图通过加重员工负担来掩盖其结构性问题。

(Similarly, chronically making overtime is a sign of a dysfunctional manager who tries to cover his effectiveness problem with throwing more time and energy at problems which do not need it. )

（同样，长期加班也是管理不善的标志，管理者试图通过投入更多的时间和精力来解决并不需要投入更多时间精力的问题来掩盖其工作效率低下的问题。）

Good managers work with their subordinates in a way that is conducive for the long-term future of both: managing their energies and their subordinates’ [5] , ensuring that both their work and the consequences of their work are sustainable, behaving from a good faith principle.

优秀的管理者与下属合作的方式有利于双方的长期未来：管理下属的精力和下属的精力[5]，确保他们的工作和工作的结果都是可持续的，并秉持诚信原则行事。

On the other hand, they are also relentless in making clear to subordinates of theirs who are not willing to adopt the same long-term collaboration principles that either they do embrace them or it is better to part ways, to save everyone’s time.

另一方面，他们也毫不含糊地向不愿接受同样长期合作原则的下属明确表示，要么接受这些原则，要么最好分道扬镳，以节省大家的时间。

Good performance management is progressive

良好的绩效管理是渐进式的。

It is common for managers to find themselves with one or more underperforming subordinates. In this case, it is extremely important that managers apply a progressive approach to performance management. Immediately setting ambitious goals would not be effective, for the underperforming subordinates might think that they are practically unreachable for them and thus react with indifference.

管理者经常会遇到一位或多位表现不佳的下属。在这种情况下，管理者采取循序渐进的绩效管理方法至关重要。立即设定过高的目标并不会奏效，因为表现不佳的下属可能会认为这些目标遥不可及，从而表现得漠不关心。

Indifference and laziness are symptoms of having forgotten that good outcomes follow good performance.

冷漠和懒惰是忘记了好的表现会带来好的结果的症状。

There are two main reasons for this amnesia: first, having been taught by previous managers that good performance is unrewarded (or that bad performance goes unpunished) and second, having lost confidence in one’s own capacity to produce satisfactory levels of performance.

这种失忆症主要有两个原因：第一，被之前的管理者灌输了“好的表现不会得到奖励（或者坏的表现不会受到惩罚）”的观念；第二，对自己能否取得令人满意的业绩失去了信心。

When facing an indifferent subordinate, the manager should teach him again that good outcomes follow good performance and that such good performance is attainable for him. The manager does not need to teach a demotivated subordinate to produce results; he needs to teach him that producing results brings good individual outcomes. These are two completely different concepts, and a manager focusing his efforts on the former while the bottleneck is the latter is setting himself up for frustration.

面对态度冷漠的下属，管理者应该再次强调，良好的表现会带来良好的结果，而良好的表现是可以实现的。管理者不需要教导一个缺乏动力的下属如何取得业绩，而是需要让他明白，取得业绩会带来良好的个人结果。这是两个截然不同的概念，如果管理者将精力集中在前者上，而忽略了后者，最终只会徒增挫败感。

(Of course, in case skills are the factor limiting the performance of the subordinate, and not motivation, then the manager will have to focus on ensuring he gets the required know-how.)

（当然，如果限制下属绩效的因素是技能而非积极性，那么经理就必须专注于确保下属获得所需的技能。）

The right way to address an indifferent subordinate is by setting small, attainable objectives and using words of appreciation (or just a simple thank you) when they achieve it. The manager has to create the conditions to be able to “catch the subordinate doing something good” and rewarding him with words for it. If done consistently enough for a few weeks, progress will inevitably follow.

对付态度冷漠的下属，正确的方法是设定一些小的、可实现的目标，并在他们达成目标时给予赞赏（或者仅仅是一句简单的“谢谢”）。管理者必须创造条件，以便“发现下属的闪光点”，并用言语表达奖励。如果坚持几周，进步必然会随之而来。

Once the subordinate begins learning that good performance is attainable and rewarded, the manager should progressively raise the objectives and the expectations regarding his performance.

一旦下属开始明白良好的表现是可以实现的，并且会得到奖励，经理就应该逐步提高对他的表现的目标和期望。

If done correctly and consistently, the previously indifferent employee will reach a sustainable state of high performance and motivation.

如果方法正确且持续，原本漠不关心的员工将达到持续的高绩效和高积极性状态。

Objectives and alignment

目标与方向

Bad managers try to reach alignment through communication; good managers achieve alignment by rewarding the behaviors which are aligned with the objectives of the organization and by punishing those who go against it.

糟糕的管理者试图通过沟通达成一致；优秀的管理者通过奖励与组织目标一致的行为，并惩罚那些违背组织目标的行为来实现一致。

# ↩


Management debt

管理债务

Whenever a manager takes the “easy choice” and sacrifices clarity, fairness or consistency to avoid a difficult conversation or a difficult choice, he incurs “management debt”: a subjective short-term gain which will eventually have to be paid back with interest.

每当一位经理为了避免艰难的谈话或艰难的选择而选择“最简单的做法”，牺牲清晰度、公平性或一致性时，他就会背负“管理债务”：一种主观的短期收益，最终必须连本带利地偿还。

Management debt happens because employees adapt negatively to the lack of clarity, fairness or consistency. As both the negative consequences of taking the easy choices and the positive consequences of taking the hard ones seem now less certain, they react with taking easy choices themselves.

管理债务的产生是因为员工对缺乏清晰度、公平性和一致性的管理方式产生了消极的适应性。由于选择轻松道路的负面后果和选择艰难道路的正面后果都变得不确定，他们便会选择选择轻松的道路。

The more the manager takes “easy choices” by sacrificing clarity, fairness or consistency, the more his subordinates will take “easy choices” themselves by sacrificing performance, quality and teamwork.

经理越是选择“容易的选择”，牺牲清晰度、公平性或一致性，他的下属就越会选择“容易的选择”，牺牲绩效、质量和团队合作。

Management Debt is an expression coined by investment firm A16Z cofounder Ben Horowitz. In his book “The Hard Thing About Hard Things”, Ben lists three sources of management debt: putting two people in the same position of the organizational chart (“putting two in the box”), overcompensating a key employee because he got another job offer, and no performance management or employee feedback process. These three sources can be respectively mapped to lack of clarity, lack of fairness and lack of consistency, as explained in the table below.

“管理债务”一词由投资公司A16Z联合创始人本·霍洛维茨提出。在他的著作《创业维艰》中，本列举了管理债务的三个来源：将两个人放在组织架构图的同一位置（“把两个人放在同一个盒子里”）、因关键员工获得其他工作机会而给予其过高的薪酬，以及缺乏绩效管理或员工反馈机制。如下表所示，这三个来源分别对应着缺乏清晰度、缺乏公平性和缺乏一致性。

# ↩


Source of management debt

管理债务来源

Corresponds to…

对应于……

Explanation

解释

Putting two in the box

把两个放进盒子里

Lack of clarity

缺乏清晰度
