Good managers know that only inconsistent judgement or judgement on unclear objectives can be perceived as unfair. Consistent judgment on unambiguous objectives whose specifics have been clear since the beginning cannot be unfair.

优秀的管理者明白，只有前后矛盾的判断或基于不明确目标的判断才会被视为不公平。而基于从一开始就明确具体目标的、前后一致的判断，则不可能是不公平的。

An inconsistent application of rules, including “good faith exceptions”, opens the doors to thoughts such as “I have been judged unfairly”, “this rule is unfair”, “this rule is wrong” and “my manager has something against me”. All this thoughts will harm future performance and team chemistry.

规则执行不一致，包括“善意例外”，会引发诸如“我受到了不公平的评判”、“这条规则不公平”、“这条规则是错误的”以及“我的经理对我有偏见”之类的想法。所有这些想法都会损害未来的工作表现和团队凝聚力。

Instead, applying rules consistently without exception focuses the employees on how they can achieve better results.

相反，始终如一地执行规则，不加例外，会让员工专注于如何取得更好的业绩。

A side advantage of applying rules consistently is that people who do not agree with them will be fast to quit the job or avoid being hired, saving both the employer and themselves a waste of time.

始终如一地执行规则的一个附带好处是，不认同这些规则的人会很快辞职或避免被录用，从而为雇主和他们自己节省时间。

Good managers choose appropriate rewards and punishments

优秀的管理者会选择合适的奖惩措施。

Managers have a whole range of tools at their disposal to apply individual outcomes to the actions of their subordinates: words of appreciation, letters of merit, one-time bonuses, promotions, assignments to better projects, enrollment to trainings, honest feedback, verbal warnings, formal warnings, disciplinary letters, and many more.

管理者可以利用各种工具来对下属的行为进行个人奖励：表扬信、嘉奖信、一次性奖金、晋升、安排到更好的项目、参加培训、诚实的反馈、口头警告、正式警告、纪律处分信等等。

Managers should select the most appropriate reward or punishment based on the magnitude of the consequence of the action of the subordinate. For example, a “thank you” should be sufficient to reward an employee who successfully completed a small objective, whereas the same would not be sufficient to reward an employee who introduced an amelioration to the production process which is saving hundreds of thousands of dollars per year to the company – a sizeable financial bonus and a letter of merit should be the bare minimum.

管理者应根据下属行为后果的严重程度选择最合适的奖惩措施。例如，对于成功完成一项小任务的员工，一句“谢谢”就足够了；但对于改进生产流程、每年为公司节省数十万美元的员工，一句“谢谢”则远远不够——至少应该给予丰厚的奖金和一封表扬信。

The principle is to appropriately pair the individual outcomes to the magnitude of consequences of the objectives which have been successfully achieved (or of the consequences of trespassing a Core Value), so that each individual subordinate can feel he is being fairly treated at his current level of performance.

其原则是将个人结果与已成功实现的目标的后果（或违反核心价值观的后果）的严重程度适当地结合起来，以便每个下属都能感到自己在当前的绩效水平上受到了公平对待。

For example, someone who achieves the minimum required objective for his position should be given some words of appreciation, whereas someone who greatly exceeds his objective or who achieved a personal objective higher than most people in his position should be rewarded with a financial bonus.

例如，达到职位最低要求的人应该得到一些赞扬，而远远超出目标或达到比同职位大多数人更高的个人目标的人应该获得经济奖励。

In general, employees tolerate well being treated differently but fairly; what they do not tolerate is being treated unfairly.

一般来说，员工能够容忍受到区别对待但公平对待；他们不能容忍的是受到不公平对待。

Good managers never reward trespassing Core Values

优秀的管理者绝不会奖励违反核心价值观的行为。

Good managers never reward trespassing Core Values, even when doing so brought results, especially when doing so brought results. They know that if a good result is celebrated when it was obtained by trespassing Core Values, then it will become acceptable – or even expected – to trespass Core Values in order to achieve results.

优秀的管理者绝不会奖励违背核心价值观的行为，即使这样做带来了业绩，尤其是在业绩如此显著的情况下。他们深知，如果通过违背核心价值观取得的良好结果得到庆祝，那么为了达成目标而违背核心价值观就会变得可以接受，甚至成为一种惯例。

Good managers never reward effort (they reward results)

优秀的管理者从不奖励努力（他们奖励结果）。

If managers reward effort, eventually, their subordinates will spend their time showing effort rather than getting results. Therefore, while good managers do acknowledge effort, they never reward it. They use sentences such as: “I noticed that you worked very hard, but you did not achieve the results that I asked you, and that is what matters.”

如果管理者奖励员工的努力，最终下属会把时间花在努力上，而不是取得成果。因此，优秀的管理者虽然会认可员工的努力，但绝不会奖励。他们会说：“我注意到你非常努力，但你没有达到我要求的成果，而这才是最重要的。”

the nature of objectives

目标的性质

If your subordinates do not trust that completing the objective you assigned them will not bring positive individual outcomes, they will not treat it as an objective.

如果你的下属不相信完成你分配给他们的目标不会带来积极的个人成果，他们就不会把这个目标当作目标来对待。

If some behavior of theirs is rewarded, performing it again will become their objective.

如果他们的某种行为得到奖励，那么再次做出这种行为就会成为他们的目标。

Objectives are what influences individual outcomes.

目标是影响个人结果的因素。

Performance management is necessary to ensure that the objectives you set are internalized as objectives and acted upon.

绩效管理对于确保您设定的目标被内化为目标并付诸行动至关重要。

Good managers are specific, in order not to pass as lunatic

优秀的管理者说话都很具体，以免被人当成疯子。

Managers who reward results regardless of efforts face the risk of getting labeled as “lunatic” by subordinates who genuinely worked hard to achieve what they thought was the objective they have been assigned, only to be told that they missed the target because, while they did achieve results, they did not achieve the results that were requested from them.

不顾努力程度而只奖励结果的管理者，可能会被下属贴上“疯子”的标签。这些下属真心实意地努力工作，试图完成他们认为被分配的目标，却被告知他们没有达到目标，因为虽然他们取得了一些结果，但并没有达到管理者要求的结果。

To avoid these situations, good managers spend a considerable amount of time applying the First Principle of Operational Excellence: setting unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives. Because their objectives are unmistakable, no subordinate of theirs feels they have been judged unfairly or believe that the manager “changed his mind”.

为了避免这种情况，优秀的管理者会花费大量时间应用卓越运营的第一原则：设定明确、个性化且可奖励的目标。由于目标清晰明确，下属不会感到被不公平对待，也不会认为管理者“改变了主意”。

Good managers set high standards

优秀的管理者会设定高标准。

Entrepreneur Ben Horowitz wrote: “In good organizations, people can focus on their work and have confidence that if they get their work done, good things will happen for both the company and them personally.”

企业家本·霍洛维茨写道：“在优秀的组织中，人们可以专注于自己的工作，并相信如果他们把工作做好，公司和他们个人都会有好结果。”

Employees have the implicit but rightful expectations that if they do their work satisfactorily, good things will happen to them. For example, once in a while, raises and promotions.

员工们理所当然地认为，只要自己工作表现出色，就会得到应有的回报。例如，偶尔会获得加薪和晋升。

Bad managers set low standards. Then, they run into troubles because some of their employees will consistently meet those standards and yet no raise, promotion or increase in responsibility can be granted, because their team did not add enough value to justify additional resources being spent in compensation.

糟糕的管理者设定过低的标准。然后，他们会遇到麻烦，因为有些员工明明一直达到这些标准，却得不到加薪、晋升或增加职责，因为他们的团队创造的价值不足以证明额外投入的薪酬是合理的。

Instead, good managers set high standards. Standards high enough that, if they are met, so much value will have been added to the company that it necessarily will have the funds to grant a promotion or a raise to the well-performing employees.

相反，优秀的管理者会设定高标准。这些标准足够高，如果员工达到这些标准，就能为公司创造巨大的价值，公司必然会有足够的资金为表现优异的员工提供晋升或加薪。

Good managers set targets high enough that their completion brings enough windfall that some can be redistributed across their team.

优秀的管理者会设定足够高的目标，这样完成目标就能带来足够的收益，并将部分收益重新分配给团队成员。

Good managers are consistent in noticing when standards aren’t met

优秀的管理者会始终如一地注意到何时未能达到标准。

Good managers understand that even their best subordinates will, sometimes, do work which is not up to standard. Good managers understand that failing to notice that the work was subpar will, counterintuitively, lead to their best subordinates getting demotivated. Failing to tell them “this piece of work wasn’t up to standard” can be interpreted as their work not being important or as the manager not caring.

优秀的管理者明白，即使是最优秀的下属，有时也会做出不合格的工作。他们也明白，如果对不合格的工作视而不见，反而会打击下属的积极性。如果不告诉他们“这项工作不合格”，可能会被解读为他们的劳动不重要，或者管理者漠不关心。

Double standards are always bad for the subordinates, even when they are in their favor.

双重标准对下属来说总是不利的，即使这种双重标准对他们有利。

Instead, good managers always tell their subordinates when their work is not good enough. And they do so in a way which is motivating. They do not say: “Your work is terrible.” They say: “Your work has always been good, but in this instance, you didn’t live up to the standard. What happened?”.

相反，优秀的管理者总会在下属工作做得不够好时坦诚相告，而且他们会用一种激励的方式。他们不会说：“你的工作糟透了”，而是会说：“你一直以来工作都很好，但这次你没有达到标准。到底发生了什么？”

Good managers understand that new employees come to the company with an abundance of motivation (or of potential motivation), and that they lose it after facing events in which “the manager doesn’t care” or in which “double standards are applied”. Good managers understand that their role is not to motivate their subordinates, but in avoiding that they become demotivated. They do so by being careful not to apply double standards and by avoiding any circumstance which could be interpreted as “the manager doesn’t care” or “the manager isn’t fair.” Good managers focus on avoiding motivational losses.

优秀的管理者明白，新员工刚入职时都充满热情（或潜力无限），但如果遇到“管理者漠不关心”或“双重标准”的情况，他们的热情就会消退。优秀的管理者明白，他们的职责不是激励下属，而是避免下属失去动力。为此，他们会谨慎行事，避免双重标准，并防止任何可能被解读为“管理者漠不关心”或“管理者不公平”的情况发生。优秀的管理者专注于避免员工失去动力。

Demotivated people are not people who cannot see the upside of doing work that matter. They are people who did not receive that upside at some point of their life when they deserved it. The motivated and the demotivated are both right in their interpretation of work based on their past emotional experiences. The managers’ job is to change them, by constantly rewiring experiences.

失去动力的人并非看不到从事有意义工作的价值，而是曾经在人生某个阶段，本应获得回报却未能如愿的人。无论是积极进取还是意志消沉，他们都基于过往的情感经历，对工作做出各自的解读。管理者的职责在于通过不断重塑他们的体验，来改变他们。

Whenever a manager is not fully consistent and fair, a bit of motivation dies in each of their subordinates. And that might be their company’s most valuable asset.

如果一位管理者不能做到始终如一、公平公正，那么他/她手下每个下属的积极性都会有所下降。而这或许正是公司最宝贵的资产。

Good managers obsess about consistency

优秀的管理者非常注重一致性。

An operations manager had a problem. Mechanical parts and components were all around the floor. Employees even had trouble walking properly without stepping on something. For months, he repeated to his employees never to leave parts on the floor and to always store them properly. They never did.

一位运营经理遇到了一个难题。机械零件和组件散落在车间各处，员工甚至走路都困难，一不小心就会踩到东西。几个月来，他反复叮嘱员工切勿将零件随意丢弃在地上，务必妥善存放。但他们始终置若罔闻。

The problem was that the warehouse was too big and the manager too busy to consistently enforce the standards he asked his employees to follow. So, he decided to restrict the area of change to a single point of the warehouse, and to obsess over it. He chose the area next to a machine. He held a stand-up meeting with the employees of the warehouse and told them that the area next to the machine always had to be clear of all parts. He told them to immediately clear it. He didn’t leave the warehouse until that area had been cleared.

问题在于仓库太大，经理又太忙，无法始终如一地执行他要求员工遵守的标准。于是，他决定将变更区域限制在仓库的一个特定点，并严格把控。他选择了机器旁边的区域。他召集仓库员工开会，告诉他们机器旁边的区域必须始终保持空置，没有任何零件。他命令他们立即清理干净。直到该区域完全清空，他才离开仓库。

For the next month, he made a point of visiting the warehouse multiple times a day and, first thing there, look at the floor next to that machine to see whether it was clear. If not, he would immediately stop whatever he was doing, walk to the nearest employee, remind him that the area had to be clear, and stay there until it was. He obsessed over it.

接下来的一个月里，他每天都会多次去仓库，每次到那儿的第一件事就是查看那台机器旁边的地面是否干净。如果没有，他会立刻停下手头的一切工作，走到最近的员工面前，提醒他那片区域必须清理干净，然后一直待在那里直到清理完毕。他对这件事简直到了痴迷的程度。

After a week, the warehouse employees learned that the machine area was to be left clear.

一周后，仓库员工得知机器区域需要清空。

After two weeks, the employees began noticing that the area next to the machine was easier to walk in, and parts there were easier to find.

两周后，员工们开始注意到机器旁边的区域更容易行走，而且那里的零件也更容易找到。

After three weeks, the magic happened. The employees began to clear the other areas of the floor, of their own account.

三周后，奇迹发生了。员工们开始自发地清理楼层的其他区域。

By focusing change over a small area, obsessing over it, and letting others see the benefit of the change, the manager achieved what he couldn’t before.

通过将变革集中在一个小的领域，全身心投入其中，并让其他人看到变革的好处，这位经理实现了他以前无法实现的目标。

This is the magic of obsessive consistency. Once the workers understand that they can change faster than their manager, they will. Once they understand that if they change, good things happen, they will.

这就是坚持不懈的魔力。一旦员工明白他们可以比他们的经理更快地做出改变，他们就会改变。一旦他们明白改变会带来好的结果，他们就会改变。

Good managers know the effectiveness of obsessive consistency.

优秀的管理者深知坚持不懈的重要性。

Good managers aim to reach critical mass

优秀的管理者力求达到临界规模。

Good managers know that habits need a critical mass to form.

优秀的管理者都知道，习惯的养成需要达到一定的规模。

Some experts say that an action becomes a habit once it has been repeated for 21 straight days. Others say that an action becomes a habit once everyone in a room performs it at once.

一些专家认为，一个行为连续重复21天后就能成为习惯。另一些专家则认为，当房间里的所有人同时做同一件事时，这个行为就能成为习惯。

Both groups of experts recognize the importance of reaching a critical mass of action – both on the temporal dimension and on the social one.

两组专家都认识到，在时间维度和社会维度上，达到行动的临界规模至关重要。

Consistency is important for two reasons. First, it helps achieving that critical mass which leads to action being converted to habits in our brain. Second, lack of consistency kills habits. The first time that you allow an employee to perform below standard without consequence, you open the door to him doing it a second time or to others doing it for the first time. He and his peers will interpret is as a signal that no one cares if someone performs below standard.

保持一致性至关重要，原因有二。首先，它有助于形成临界规模，从而使行动在我们的大脑中转化为习惯。其次，缺乏一致性会扼杀习惯。如果你第一次允许员工表现低于标准而未加惩罚，就等于为他第二次犯同样的错误，或者为其他人第一次犯同样的错误敞开了大门。他和他的同事会将此解读为：没有人关心员工的表现是否达标。

It doesn’t matter whether it is true. What matters is the perception that is created.

真假并不重要，重要的是它所形成的认知。

Because good managers know the importance of reaching critical mass, they restrict the magnitude of the change to be achieved at a time. Instead of asking their subordinates to adopt 5 new habits this month, they ask them to adopt only one. Otherwise, they would have to divide their limited time between noticing, praising or reprimanding 5 habits or lack thereof. By focusing on noticing, praising or reprimanding a single habit, good managers decrease the likelihood of missing an instance in which a subordinate failed to express the required habit.

优秀的管理者深知达到临界规模的重要性，因此他们会限制每次需要实现的变革规模。他们不会要求下属本月养成五种新习惯，而是只要求一种。否则，他们就不得不将有限的时间分散在观察、表扬或批评五种习惯的养成与否上。通过专注于观察、表扬或批评单一习惯，优秀的管理者可以降低错过下属未能养成所需习惯的情况的概率。

Because they know the importance of reaching critical mass, good managers restrict the number of people that must adopt a new habit at a given time. Instead of requiring their whole building to adopt a new habit, they focus on one or two teams at a time. This way, they won’t have to spread their attention too thin. They ensure that no bad habit will go unnoticed, and no good habit unreinforced. They know that employees watch how their colleagues are treated. If they see a colleague failing to adopt a new habit and nothing happening, they will learn that they can do the same. Good managers, by obsessing over a single new habit of a small group of people at a time, ensure that no such occurrence takes place.

优秀的管理者深知达到临界规模的重要性，因此他们会限制每次需要养成新习惯的人数。他们不会要求整栋楼的员工都养成新习惯，而是每次只专注于一到两个团队。这样一来，他们就不必分散精力。他们确保任何坏习惯都不会被忽视，任何好习惯也不会被遗漏。他们知道员工会观察同事的待遇。如果他们看到同事未能养成新习惯却无人问津，他们就会认为自己也可以效仿。优秀的管理者通过每次专注于一小群人养成一个新习惯，确保这种情况不会发生。

The tricky part

棘手的部分

The tricky part about the Fourth Principle of Operational Excellence is that it won’t begin to work when you begin to use it; it will begin to work when there is no instance in which you don’t apply it.

卓越运营第四原则的棘手之处在于，它不会在你开始使用它时就开始起作用；它只有在你处处都应用它时才会开始起作用。

Summary

概括

Good managers find the time to consistently reinforce change by restricting it to a single new habit and a few new people at a time.

优秀的管理者会抽出时间，通过每次只引入一个新习惯和少数几个新人来不断强化变革。

They find the energy to do so by acknowledging that consistency is the most important attribute of a good manager.

他们之所以能做到这一点，是因为他们认识到，持之以恒是优秀管理者最重要的品质。

Great companies promote consistency of management as a Core Value and make it trickle down from the top through costly tradeoffs performed by the Leadership, thus ensuring that no manager misunderstands its importance

优秀的公司将管理一致性作为核心价值观来推崇，并通过领导层做出代价高昂的权衡取舍，使其自上而下地贯彻执行，从而确保每位管理者都充分理解其重要性。

Good managers are fair, not loyal. Workers say that they want loyal bosses, but what they really want is fair ones. This because someone cannot be loyal to everyone at all times, but he can be fair to everyone every time.

优秀的管理者公正，而非忠诚。员工口口声声说想要忠诚的老板，但他们真正想要的其实是公正的老板。这是因为一个人不可能永远对所有人忠诚，但他可以始终对所有人公正。

# ↩

Paradigm shifts

范式转变

The Four Principles of Operational Excellence introduce four paradigm shifts.

卓越运营的四大原则引入了四项范式转变。

The First Principle introduced a paradigm shift from “understanding objectives is the subordinate’s responsibility” to “assigning unmistakable objectives is the manager’s responsibility.”

第一原则引入了一种范式转变，从“理解目标是下属的责任”转变为“设定明确的目标是管理者的责任”。

The Second Principle introduced a paradigm shift from “compliance brings results” to “compliance alone doesn’t bring results; accountability to results does.”

第二原则引入了一种范式转变，从“合规带来结果”转变为“单靠合规并不能带来结果；对结果负责才能带来结果”。

The Third Principle introduced a paradigm shift from “management has to be efficient” to “signals must be costly to be effective.”

第三原则引入了一种范式转变，从“管理必须高效”转变为“信号必须有成本才能有效”。

The Fourth Principle introduce a paradigm shift from “taking right decisions is a matter of pragmatism” to “whether a decision is right is determined by how it will influence the future behavior of employees.”

第四原则引入了一种范式转变，从“做出正确的决定是实用主义的问题”转变为“一个决定是否正确取决于它将如何影响员工未来的行为”。

# ↩

The Role of The Manager

经理的角色

Before moving on to the Eight Best Practices, it is worth spending a few pages on the role of the manager.

在介绍八项最佳实践之前，有必要花几页篇幅谈谈经理的角色。

Good managers are proactive

优秀的管理者积极主动。

“Lead proactively, do not manager reactively.”
– Keith Rabois

“要积极主动地领导，而不是被动地管理。”——基思·拉博伊斯

Good managers do their job well today, because yesterday they planted the seed for effective management: clarity.

优秀的管理者今天之所以能做好工作，是因为他们昨天播下了有效管理的种子：清晰的思路。

Bad managers take decisions based on how they influence their world today. Good managers take decisions based on how they influence the future behavior of their subordinates.

糟糕的管理者根据决策对当下环境的影响来做决定。优秀的管理者则根据决策对下属未来行为的影响来做决定。

Leverage

杠杆作用

Doing the work of one of your subordinates is a low-leverage action: spending ten minutes of your time creating the same output as ten minutes of your subordinate’s time.

替下属做工作是一种低杠杆行为：花十分钟时间创造的产出与下属花十分钟时间创造的产出相同。

Training is a high-leverage activity. If you spend 1% of your time training your 8 subordinates so that their output improves by 1% each, your action had an 8x leverage.

培训是一项高杠杆活动。如果你花1%的时间培训你的8名下属，使他们的产出每人提高1%，那么你的行动就产生了8倍的杠杆效应。

The higher the leverage of the activities you spend your time on, the higher your contribution to the effectiveness of your team.

你投入时间的活动的杠杆作用越高，你对团队效率的贡献就越大。

Avoid spending your time in low-leverage activities (your subordinates’ job, reports, etc.) and spend it on high-leverage ones: long-term decisions, training, improving clarity, preventing motivational losses.

避免把时间浪费在低效活动（下属的工作、报告等）上，而应该把时间花在高效活动上：长期决策、培训、提高清晰度、防止士气低落。

Overcommunication

过度沟通

You only communicated something when it feels you overcommunicated it. Managers are smart people who do not want to question the smartness of their subordinates by repeating. Therefore, the expectation that managers must overcommunicate has to be made explicit to avoid politeness getting in the way of effectiveness.

只有当你感觉沟通过度时，才算是真正有效地沟通了。管理者都是聪明人，他们不希望通过重复来质疑下属的聪明才智。因此，必须明确指出管理者需要进行充分沟通，以避免礼貌妨碍工作效率。

I like management consultant Patrick Lencioni’s definition of overcommunication [12] : “ employees understand how they contribute to the success of their organization. They do not spend time speculating on what executives are really thinking.”

我喜欢管理顾问帕特里克·兰西奥尼对过度沟通的定义[12]：“员工明白他们如何为组织的成功做出贡献。他们不会花时间去猜测高管们到底在想什么。”

Don’t feel bad repeating yourself, it is worth it.

不要觉得重复自己很不好意思，这样做是值得的。

Overcommunication has to be costly: a footnote in a slide deck won’t do. Show up in person.

过度沟通必然要付出代价：幻灯片上的脚注是远远不够的。务必亲自到场。

Making the important conspicuous

使重要的事情引人注目

During the discussion of the Four Principles of Operational Excellence, a great deal of emphasis has been placed on making the important conspicuous: making sure that everyone knows the important (Core Values and their uncompromisability, their personal objectives, the fact that individual outcomes will inevitably be applied to them based on their performance against those objectives) and making sure that everyone knows that everyone else knows it as well.

在讨论卓越运营的四大原则时，人们非常强调要突出重点：确保每个人都知道重要的事情（核心价值观及其不可妥协性、个人目标、个人结果将不可避免地根据他们实现这些目标的表现而应用于他们），并确保每个人都知道其他人也知道这些。

Your main tasks as a manager are making the important unmistakable and conspicuous, and consistently rewarding people based on their result against their personal objectives and on stewarding Core Values.

作为管理者，你的主要任务是使重要的事情明确无误、引人注目，并根据员工实现个人目标的成果和对核心价值观的践行，持续地给予奖励。

Communicating meaning

传达意义

Employees work well when they work on something meaningful and they know it.

员工在从事有意义的工作并且了解这项工作时，工作效率会很高。

Almost any job is meaningful, for it enables others to enjoy products and services. For example, in a memorable 1960 speech to Hewlett-Packard employees, cofounder David Packard said “in those areas where we are making instruments, we are supplying about one third of the country's total requirements […] it indicates that we have a responsibility, in that we are making a very major contribution to the total technical effort of this country. Your efforts are not only worthwhile but you are doing something which is really significant in terms of total technical effort. You have seen photographs of important scientific work being done – and those photos include HP instruments. Those of you who visit the labs of our customers find our instruments are being used in very important work; the advancement of science, defense of our country, and many other areas. So, don't overlook our responsibility.”

几乎任何工作都意义非凡，因为它能让其他人享受到产品和服务。例如，在1960年惠普公司联合创始人戴维·帕卡德对员工发表的一次令人难忘的演讲中，他说道：“在我们生产仪器的领域，我们供应了全国约三分之一的需求……这表明我们肩负着重大的责任，因为我们为国家的整体技术发展做出了非常重要的贡献。你们的努力不仅值得，而且就整体技术发展而言，你们所做的事情意义重大。你们都见过一些重要科学研究的照片——其中就包括惠普的仪器。你们当中那些参观过我们客户实验室的人会发现，我们的仪器被用于非常重要的工作中：推动科学进步、保卫国家以及许多其他领域。所以，请不要忽视我们的责任。”

You can do the same as Mr. Packard did in his speech above: explain to your subordinates how the products of your organization contribute to the life of their users.

你可以像帕卡德先生在上面的演讲中那样做：向你的下属解释你所在组织的产品如何为用户的生活做出贡献。

Do not assume that your subordinates already know how their efforts contribute to others, and do not assume that telling them is an insult to their intelligence. People need to be explicitly reminded of the worth of their efforts, even if they know it already. They need to be reminded every month, so that once they have a bad day, frustration does not find any fertile ground to grow onto.

不要想当然地认为你的下属已经明白他们的努力对他人有何贡献，也不要认为告诉他们是在侮辱他们的智商。即使人们已经意识到自己努力的价值，也需要被明确地提醒。他们需要每月都得到这样的提醒，这样，即使遇到不顺心的事情，也不会让沮丧的情绪滋生蔓延。

It is the job of managers and supervisors to let their subordinates know about the meaning of their work in an emotional way : what emotions do the products produced by your organization create in their users, directly or indirectly?

经理和主管的职责是让下属以情感的方式了解他们工作的意义：你的组织生产的产品直接或间接地给用户带来了哪些情感？

As a manager, it is your job to help your subordinates understand the meaning of their work and to ensure that they are, in turn, helping their own subordinates do the same.

作为管理者，你的职责是帮助下属理解他们工作的意义，并确保他们反过来也帮助他们的下属做到这一点。

Good managers are aware of how employees adapt

优秀的管理者了解员工如何适应

A good manager knows that employees mostly react to the incentives, explicit or implicit, that they have been trained to expect as per their individual experience.

优秀的管理者知道，员工大多会对他们根据自身经验所期望的、明确的或隐含的激励措施做出反应。

Therefore, a good manager takes actions not for their direct result, but for how his subordinates will adapt to them.

因此，优秀的管理者采取行动并非着眼于行动的直接结果，而是着眼于下属将如何适应这些行动。

He knows that every time he applies fair individual outcomes to his subordinates’ performance, they adapt, in the right direction.

他知道，每当他用公平的个人结果来评价下属的绩效时，他们都会朝着正确的方向做出调整。

He also knows that every time he fails to do so, they adapt as well; this time, in the wrong direction.

他也知道，每次他不这样做，他们也会随之调整；这一次，调整的方向却错了。

Therefore, he is obsessively consistent in holding them accountable for their performance; and he does so without remorse, because he set humane objectives and he has been unmistakably clear about what they represent.

因此，他执着地要求他们对自己的表现负责；而且他毫不后悔，因为他设定了人道的目标，并且明确地说明了这些目标的意义。

Good managers communicate incentives

优秀的管理者会沟通激励措施。

Good managers know that values are downstream of incentives and, therefore, to communicate values they need to communicate incentives.

优秀的管理者知道价值观是激励机制的下游产物，因此，要传达价值观，他们需要先传达激励机制。

Consequently, they are relentless in reinforcing the behaviors of those who steward Core Values and in punishing those who trespass them, regardless of their intention and of their short-term contribution to the bottom line.

因此，无论意图如何，也无论对公司短期业绩有何贡献，公司都会毫不留情地强化那些践踏核心价值观的人的行为，并惩罚那些违反核心价值观的人。

# ↩


Good managers are in for the long run

优秀的管理者着眼于长远发展。

Good managers know that employee turnover is bad, both from a personal point of view (it takes time to know another person, to build trust, to learn how to manage him or her effectively, to learn to appreciate his or her work, to integrate him or her in the team) and from the operational point of view (it takes time to find, hire and train a new employee and for him to learn how to work effectively in his new role, team and company).

优秀的管理者都知道员工流动率高是不好的，无论从个人角度（需要时间去了解另一个人，建立信任，学习如何有效地管理他或她，学会欣赏他或她的工作，将其融入团队）还是从运营角度（需要时间去寻找、雇用和培训一名新员工，并让他学习如何在新角色、新团队和新公司中有效地工作）来看都是如此。

Therefore, good managers take care of removing as many reasons as possible for which employees leave due to frustration:

因此，优秀的管理者会尽力消除员工因沮丧而离职的各种原因：

  • Useless effort: employees receive motivational losses when they were expecting a reward or acknowledgement for their work and did not receive it (because the manager is too busy or because the manager didn’t set a clear enough objective so that there is a misunderstanding about what constitutes a satisfactory result) or when they produce an output which is later shown not to contribute to the success of the team or of the company (e.g., they worked for a week on a report no one will read).
    徒劳的努力：员工期望因其工作而获得奖励或认可，但却没有得到（因为经理太忙，或者因为经理没有设定足够明确的目标，导致对令人满意的结果的定义产生误解），或者当他们产出的产品后来被证明对团队或公司的成功没有贡献时（例如，他们花了一周时间写了一份没人会看的报告），就会遭受积极性损失。
  • Unfairness: employees receive motivational losses whenever they feel they are treated unfairly – for example, when they see that an employee providing less value is paid more than them or when they take the time to follow effortful procedures and another employee skipping them is not reprimanded. Of course, sometimes such resentment is unmotivated – for example, when the better-paid employee is providing value that they cannot see – but in this case it is almost exclusively because the manager did not do a good job of setting a clear and conspicuous picture of what a good result looks like, so that there could be agreement about who is providing value and how much.
    不公平：员工一旦感到受到不公平对待，就会降低工作积极性——例如，当他们看到贡献更少的员工薪水更高，或者当他们花费时间认真完成繁琐的流程，而其他员工偷工减料却未受到任何惩罚时。当然，有时这种不满并非出于本能——例如，当薪水更高的员工创造了他们看不到的价值时——但这种情况几乎完全是因为管理者没有清晰明确地定义“好结果”的标准，导致员工无法就谁在创造价值以及价值的大小达成共识。

The First, Second and Fourth Principle of Operational Excellence are about being so clear in setting objectives and consistent in rewarding them that the two sources of motivational losses described above won’t apply to your subordinates.

卓越运营的第一、第二和第四原则是：在设定目标时要非常明确，在奖励目标时要始终如一，这样上述两种激励损失的来源就不会适用于你的下属。

Similarly, good managers are also effective at removing the root causes that lead to employees leaving the organization due to burnout:

同样，优秀的管理者也能有效地消除导致员工因职业倦怠而离职的根本原因：

  • Chronic overwork: as mentioned in the introduction, whereas occasional periods of increased workload are normal and signal a healthy business, chronic overwork is a symptom of structural problems.
    长期过度劳累：正如引言中所述，偶尔的工作量增加是正常的，表明企业运营健康，而长期过度劳累则是结构性问题的征兆。
  • Unrewarded overwork: overwork which brings rewards – a bonus, a sense of accomplishment, etc. – generally does not cause burnout, except in the most extreme cases, but overwork which doesn’t bring rewards does cause burnout, and rather quickly. A specific case of burnout-causing overwork is the one which is potentially rewarded, but the performance threshold to get these rewards is so high that it is either too consuming or too unattainable.
    无回报的过度工作：如果过度工作能带来奖励——例如奖金、成就感等等——通常不会导致职业倦怠，除非在极少数极端情况下。但如果过度工作没有带来任何回报，则会导致职业倦怠，而且速度相当快。一种会导致职业倦怠的过度工作情况是：虽然有可能获得奖励，但获得这些奖励的绩效门槛过高，要么过于耗费精力，要么根本无法达到。

Therefore, good managers make sure that they do not cause their subordinates to do chronic overwork and that when they cause them to undergo occasional spikes of workload, they appropriately reward them for it.

因此，优秀的管理者会确保不让下属长期过度工作，并且当他们偶尔面临工作量激增时，会给予适当的奖励。

Please note that I did not use the words “ask”, but “cause”. This is because managers cannot hide behind the excuse of “I never asked my subordinates to work overtime, they just happen to do so.” Chronic overwork is the symptom of either a bad business, a lack of willingness to hire enough employees, a lack of willingness to train them effectively or a lack of effectiveness in managing them – and these are all responsibilities of the management.

请注意，我没有使用“要求”，而是使用了“导致”。这是因为管理者不能再用“我从未要求下属加班，他们只是碰巧加班而已”这样的借口来推卸责任。长期过度劳累要么是企业经营不善的表现，要么是企业不愿招聘足够员工、不愿进行有效培训或管理不善的表现——而这些都是管理层的责任。

Do not project

不要投影

I’ve seen many managers becoming an issue for their team by projecting their own problems and insecurities on them. Perhaps it’s you too. Or perhaps not. Either way, when you have a problem, work on it yourself or with your own manager; do not project it on your team.

我见过很多管理者因为把自己的问题和不安全感投射到团队身上而成为团队的负担。也许你也是这样，也许不是。无论如何，当你遇到问题时，应该自己解决或者和你的上司沟通解决；不要把问题转嫁给团队。

Things Bad managers do

糟糕的管理者会做的事

Bad managers spend time on unimportant things or on things one of their subordinates could take care of.

糟糕的管理者会把时间浪费在不重要的事情上，或者浪费在下属可以处理的事情上。

Bad managers proud themselves of their problems; they focus on signaling busyness and effort over effectiveness.

糟糕的管理者会以自己的问题为荣；他们更注重展现忙碌和努力，而不是效率。

Bad managers project their problems over their subordinates, to the point that they see them as problems rather than opportunities.

糟糕的管理者会将自己的问题投射到下属身上，以至于下属把他们视为问题而不是机会。

Bad managers do whatever it takes to achieve short-term results.

糟糕的管理者会不择手段地追求短期业绩。

Bad managers are pragmatic and ready to compromise Core Values if the payoff is large enough.

糟糕的管理者务实，如果回报足够大，他们就准备在核心价值观上妥协。

Bad managers are more competent than their subordinates at their subordinates’ jobs.

糟糕的管理者比他们的下属更擅长他们的工作。

Things good managers do

优秀经理人会做的事

Good managers obsess over figuring out which objectives and behaviors are important for the long-term success of the organization, focusing everyone’s attention on them and then rewarding them for turning them into reality.

优秀的管理者会专注于找出对组织长期成功至关重要的目标和行为，让每个人都关注这些目标和行为，然后奖励那些将这些目标和行为变为现实的人。

Good managers ignore noise and instead focus on signal in everything they do, in everything they pay attention to, in everything they punish and in everything they reward.

优秀的管理者会忽略噪音，而将注意力集中在他们所做的每一件事、他们关注的每件事、他们惩罚的每件事和他们奖励的每件事上。

Good managers are obsessed stewards of Core Values.

优秀的管理者是核心价值观的忠实守护者。

# ↩

Conclusions of Part I

第一部分结论

Operational Excellence is about selecting, reinforcing and sustaining in your team those mental patterns which are conducive to autonomous individual action which is aligned with the long-term objectives of your organization.

卓越运营是指在你的团队中选择、强化和维持那些有利于自主个人行动的思维模式，这些行动与组织的长期目标保持一致。

Setting unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives, unmistakably delegating full accountability, taking costly actions and being obsessively consistent is most of what you need to focus on.

设定明确、个性化且可奖励的目标，明确委派全部责任，采取代价高昂的行动，并坚持不懈地努力，这就是你需要关注的大部分内容。

Only this way, you will avoid creating fertile ground for motivational losses and for circumstances which will dilute your authority and your organization’s Operational Culture.

只有这样，你才能避免为士气低落和削弱你的权威及组织运营文化创造滋生的土壤。

# ↩

Part II:
第二部分：
Best Practices
最佳实践

In the first part of this book, I presented the Four Principles of Operational Excellence.

本书第一部分介绍了卓越运营的四大原则。

1) Good managers set unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives.

1）优秀的管理者会设定明确、个人化且可奖励的目标。

2) Good managers always explicitly assign full accountability together with objectives.

2）优秀的管理者总是明确地将全部责任与目标结合起来。

3) Good managers demonstrate priorities with visible costly actions.

3) 优秀的管理者会通过看得见的、代价高昂的行动来表明优先事项。

4) Good managers are obsessively consistent in holding their subordinates accountable.

4）优秀的管理者会坚持不懈地要求下属承担责任。

In the second part of this book, I will present the Eight Best Practices which good managers use to transform those principles into visible actions .

本书第二部分将介绍优秀管理者将这些原则转化为可见行动的八项最佳实践。

The reason they are called Best Practice s is that they have to be practiced, over and over, week over week, for the organization to benefit from it. Just like physical fitness is not something that takes care of itself once it is achieved but requires a constant practice at the gym or doing your favorite sport, Operational Excellence requires a constant practice of the following 8 activities.

之所以称之为最佳实践，是因为它们必须反复实践，每周持续进行，组织才能从中受益。正如身体素质并非一蹴而就，而是需要持续在健身房锻炼或进行自己喜欢的运动一样，卓越运营也需要持续实践以下8项活动。

# ↩

Best Practice #1:
最佳实践#1：

Management Walks
管理层巡视

If a manager does not know what goes on in his own Operations, he will not be able to manage them properly. If the subordinates of a manager do not see him spending time where Operations take place, they will not trust that he can manage them properly. For these two reasons, it is critical that managers spend time where the work they manage takes place.

如果一位管理者不了解自己部门的运营情况，他就无法有效地管理这些部门。如果一位管理者的下属看不到他花时间在运营现场，他们就不会信任他能够妥善管理他们。正因如此，管理者花时间了解自己所管理的工作至关重要。

The Toyota Production System (TPS) has a term for this, Genchi Genbutsu – “Go and See”. According to the TPS, in order to truly understand a situation, one needs to go to “genba” – the “real place” where work is done.

丰田生产系统（TPS）对此有一个术语：现地现物（Genchi Genbutsu），意为“亲临现场”。根据TPS的理念，为了真正了解情况，需要前往“现场”（genba），即工作实际发生的“真实场所”。

However, getting a practical knowledge of operations and being seen getting a practical knowledge of operations are only two of the three reasons why good managers spend time at the place where work is done. Taking visible actions is the third one.

然而，获得实际操作经验以及让别人看到自己获得了实际操作经验，只是优秀管理者花时间在工作现场的三个原因中的两个。采取切实可见的行动是第三个原因。

Decisions taken in the managers’ office remain in there. They do not have the power to affect how their subordinates work unless the manager translates them into visible actions at their subordinates’ workplace.

经理办公室里做出的决定仅限于办公室内部，除非经理将这些决定转化为下属工作场所中可见的行动，否则这些决定无权影响下属的工作方式。

In order to do that, good managers use Management Walks.

为了做到这一点，优秀的管理者会采用管理巡视的方式。

# ↩


Management walks

管理层巡视

Management Walks are regular instances in which a manager takes the time to physically walk where his subordinates spend their time. This includes both their direct subordinates and, most importantly, everyone else below them. Even the CEO, to be a good manager, should spend at least one hour a month on the factory shop floor, observing the workers there and directly interacting with them with visible actions to show them what the priorities of the company are.

管理巡视是指管理者定期抽出时间，实地走访下属们日常工作和生活的地方。这不仅包括直接下属，更重要的是，还包括所有级别低于他们的员工。即使是首席执行官，要想成为一名优秀的管理者，也应该每月至少花一个小时在工厂车间，观察工人的工作，并通过实际行动与他们互动，向他们展示公司的优先事项。

Other Operational Excellence systems have similar practices called “Gemba Walks”, “Line Walks” or “Observations”.

其他卓越运营体系也有类似的做法，称为“现场巡视”、“生产线巡视”或“观察”。

What happens during a Management Walk?

管理层巡视期间会发生什么？

During a management walk, the manager performs the following set of steps:

在管理巡视过程中，经理会执行以下步骤：

  1. He walks near where the workers are working and silently observes them. He takes care of following all required procedures (e.g., safety procedures such as wearing a helmet), in order to set the good example and to convey the message that no one is exempt from following them.
    他走到工人们工作的地方附近，默默地观察他们。他严格遵守所有必要的程序（例如，佩戴安全帽等安全规程），以身作则，并传达这样一个信息：任何人都没有例外，必须遵守这些规程。
  2. He tries to catch something good, something bad, or something he does not understand. “Good” and “bad” refer to having followed the rules and the Core Value s of the company.
    他试图捕捉到好的、坏的，或者他无法理解的东西。“好”和“坏”指的是是否遵守了公司的规则和核心价值观。
  3. If he notices something good, the manager personally thanks the worker for having done it.
    如果经理注意到员工做得好的地方，他会亲自感谢员工。
  4. If he notices something he doesn’t understand, the manager asks explanations to the nearest worker. He is careful to adopt a posture of humility and openness. He avoids making any suggestion before having fully understood why things are done the way they are.
    如果他发现有什么不明白的地方，这位经理会向最近的员工询问。他总是保持谦逊和开放的态度。在完全了解事情运作的原因之前，他不会轻易提出任何建议。
  5. If he notices something bad, he walks to the worker who is working in a way which breaks the procedures, rules or Core Values of the company. He politely interrupts him when it is safe to do so and asks him why he is acting the way he is. Perhaps there is a good explanation. A good manager doesn’t assume that he knows better than his employees, unless he ascertained so. If there is a good explanation for the behavior breaking the rules and procedures, then the rules and procedures must be rewritten to accommodate the circumstance. Otherwise, the behavior cannot be excused. The manager proceeds to remind the employee the proper way of working and asks him to immediately comply with action . This way, he can verify correct understanding and allow a physical habit to form in the mind of the subordinate. Finally, the manager thanks the worker for his time and collaboration.
    如果他发现有不妥之处，他会走到那位违反公司流程、规则或核心价值观的员工面前。在确保自身安全的情况下，他会礼貌地打断员工，询问其行为原因。或许员工有合理的解释。一位优秀的管理者不会自以为比员工更懂，除非他已经确认了这一点。如果员工违反规则和流程的行为有合理的解释，那么就必须修改规则和流程以适应具体情况。否则，这种行为就不能被原谅。管理者会提醒员工正确的操作方法，并要求其立即执行。这样，他既可以确认员工是否真正理解，又能让员工养成良好的习惯。最后，管理者感谢员工的时间和配合。

It is important to note that the manager should not let any behavior which violates rules, procedures or Core Values untouched. Either the rule or procedure has to be rewritten, or the worker has to acknowledge he shouldn’t have acted that way. There is no grey area in between, no one-off exception. Letting an exception pass once is how exceptions become the new norm. Good managers never allow that.

值得注意的是，管理者绝不应放任任何违反规则、流程或核心价值观的行为不管。要么修改规则或流程，要么员工必须承认自己的行为不当。没有中间地带，也没有例外。放任例外一次，就会让例外变成新的常态。优秀的管理者绝不会允许这种情况发生。

Begin with openness to the possibility that the rule is wrong but, once you ascertained that it is not, be categorically inflexible in its application.

首先要对规则可能出错的可能性持开放态度，但一旦确定规则是正确的，就应该在应用时毫不妥协。

In case the worker had a good reason to act the way he did, and the rule or procedure has to be rewritten, the act of immediately ordering the rule or procedure to be rewritten is a Visible Action that shows that exceptions cannot exist. Either the rule or procedure is always right or it is wrong. No such thing as “a procedure to follow most of the times” should be allowed.

如果该员工有正当理由采取其行为，且规则或程序需要修改，那么立即下令修改规则或程序本身就是一项公开的行动，表明不允许存在例外情况。规则或程序要么永远正确，要么永远错误。绝不应允许存在“大多数情况下都适用的程序”。

Who performs Management Walks?

谁负责进行管理层巡视？

Everyone, with different frequency.

每个人，频率都不一样。

Top management, including the CEO, should perform a minimum of a Management Walk a month.

包括首席执行官在内的高层管理人员每月至少应进行一次管理巡视。

Managers should perform one at least once a week.

管理者至少应该每周进行一次这样的评估。

Supervisors should perform one at least once a day.

主管人员每天至少应进行一次这样的操作。

This might seem a lot, but it is necessary to achieve Operational Excellence. OpEx trickles down from clarity and from visible example, and Management Walks are the perfect tool to cover the second part of the equation.

这看起来或许很多，但却是实现卓越运营的必要条件。卓越运营源于清晰的愿景和直观的示范，而管理巡视正是实现这一目标的理想工具。

Should workers perform walks too?

工人也应该进行步行锻炼吗？

In a company where Operational Excellence is an internalized concept, yes.

在一家将卓越运营视为内部理念的公司里，答案是肯定的。

However, if your company is still at the beginning of its journey towards Operational Excellence, it is advised that only managers perform them. Only once the line workers internalize the concept of Walks from their managers, they can be given the task to perform them as well – once a week or once a day.

然而，如果贵公司仍处于卓越运营的起步阶段，建议仅由管理人员执行巡视。只有当一线员工从管理人员那里理解并掌握了巡视的概念后，才能让他们也承担巡视的任务——每周一次或每天一次。

When line workers do the Walks, they either perform them in their own workplace (observing their teammates) or in areas adjacent to it, such as nearby production lines or warehouses. Having workers performing the Walks observing their own teammates promotes peer accountability, whereas having them performing the Walks in nearby areas allows for cross-pollination of Best Practices and prevents complacency – seeing the same workplace every day might cause them to stop noticing chronic problems and treat them as normal instead.

生产线工人进行巡视时，既可以在自己的工作场所（观察同事）进行，也可以在邻近区域进行，例如附近的生产线或仓库。让工人观察自己的同事有助于促进同伴间的相互监督，而让他们在邻近区域进行巡视则有利于最佳实践的交叉学习，并防止自满情绪的产生——每天面对同样的工作场所可能会导致他们忽视长期存在的问题，并将其视为正常现象。

What to look for during a walk?

散步时应该注意什么？

There are two categories of situations to look for during a Walk: conditions and behaviors. Some drops of oil on the floor are an unsafe condition; a worker walking on the shop floor without the safety shoes is an unsafe behavior. Similarly, a poorly maintained machine is an unsafe condition, whereas a worker using a tool the wrong way is a bad behavior.

巡视过程中需要关注两类情况：环境状况和行为。地板上的油滴属于不安全环境；工人未穿安全鞋在车间行走属于不安全行为。同样，维护不善的机器属于不安全环境，而工人错误使用工具则属于不安全行为。

Bad managers only call out bad conditions and behaviors: situations which are unsafe or otherwise wrong, according to rules, procedures, standards and Core Values. Instead, during Management Walks, good managers call out both good and bad conditions and behaviors.

糟糕的管理者只会指出不妥之处和行为：那些违反规章制度、流程、标准和核心价值观，不安全或有其他错误的情况。而优秀的管理者在巡视管理中，会同时指出好的和不好的情况和行为。

Here is a (non-exhaustive) list of common conditions to look for: are there tools out of place? Are the walkways encumbered? Is any object placed where it could fall easily? Are the shelves messy? Is the space dirty? Is there any non-labeled machine or button? Is there any unlabeled container?

以下是一些常见的需要检查的情况（并非全部）：工具是否摆放不当？通道是否拥挤？是否有物品放置在容易掉落的地方？货架是否凌乱？空间是否脏乱？是否有未贴标签的机器或按钮？是否有未贴标签的容器？

Here is a (non-exhaustive) list of common behaviors to look for: are the workers breaking safety procedures? Are they rushing? Are they multitasking? Are they walking or standing where they are not supposed to? Are they observing their mobile phone when they’re not supposed to? Are they using the wrong tools, or misusing the right ones?

以下是一些常见的违规行为（并非全部）：工人是否违反安全规程？他们是否匆忙行事？他们是否同时处理多项任务？他们是否在不该走动或站立的地方行走或站立？他们是否在不该看手机的时候查看手机？他们是否使用了错误的工具，或者错误地使用了正确的工具？

A more comprehensive checklist of conditions and behaviors to look for will be presented in the next chapter, called “Best Practice #2: Audits”.

下一章“最佳实践#2：审核”将提供一份更全面的条件和行为检查清单。

Look for both the good and the bad

既要看好，也要看坏。

Behavioral theory suggests that positive reinforcement (praising or rewarding someone for a good behavior) is more effective towards the formation of habits than negative reinforcement (reprimanding or punishing).

行为理论表明，对于习惯的养成，积极强化（表扬或奖励某人的良好行为）比消极强化（训斥或惩罚）更有效。

This does not mean that negative reinforcement is not to be used. For the sake of consistency (the Fourth Principle of Operational Excellence), a manager cannot supersede on any violation of rules, procedures, standards or Core Values. It means that, to maximize effectiveness, both positive and negative reinforcement must be used. Good managers look out for both the good and the bad, and act on both of them.

这并不意味着不能使用负强化。为了保持一致性（卓越运营的第四原则），管理者不能对任何违反规则、程序、标准或核心价值观的行为视而不见。这意味着，为了最大限度地提高效率，必须同时使用正强化和负强化。优秀的管理者会关注好的和坏的方面，并采取相应的行动。

Talking with workers

与工人交谈

Once they see a good or bad condition or behavior, managers should immediately initiate an interaction with the relevant worker. Praises and reprimands are most effective when given instantly after observing the object of the remark. In case an immediate interruption would compromise the safety of the worker, managers should wait for the first moment in which it would be safe to interrupt.

一旦发现员工的良好或不良行为，管理者应立即与相关员工进行沟通。表扬和批评在观察到相关情况后立即进行最为有效。如果立即介入会危及员工安全，管理者应等待时机，确保安全后再介入。

If the manager observed a good or bad behavior, he interacts with the worker having performed it. If the manager observed a good or bad condition, he instead interacts with the closest employee to the location where the condition has been observed. Some examples:

如果经理观察到员工有良好或不良的行为，他会与做出该行为的员工进行沟通。如果经理观察到环境状况良好或不佳，他会与距离该状况发生地点最近的员工进行沟通。例如：

- If the manager observes a sharp tool left on the floor on the walkway next to an unattended worktable, he is to interact with the worker assigned to that table.

- 如果经理发现走道上无人看管的工作台旁边的地板上遗留着锋利的工具，他应该与负责该工作台的工人进行沟通。

- If the manager observes a sharp tool left unattended on the floor on the side of the warehouse, he is to interact with the closest worker to the tool that he can see in that moment. Even if that worker is just “passing by”, to demonstrate the concept that rules, standards and Core Values are a shared responsibility. Keeping an eye open for them is everyone’s responsibility. Holding peers, subordinates and superiors accountable for rules, standards and Core Values is everyone’s responsibility.

如果经理发现仓库边地板上有无人看管的锋利工具，他应该立即与当时在场的离工具最近的员工沟通。即使该员工只是“路过”，也要这样做，以表明规则、标准和核心价值观是每个人的责任。留意这些规则、标准和核心价值观是每个人的责任。督促同事、下属和上级遵守规则、标准和核心价值观也是每个人的责任。

Some more on the last line. People are responsible both for achieving results and for stewarding Core Values. Whereas accountability for the former has to trickle down the hierarchical line (with the CEO setting the objectives for his direct subordinates and holding them accountable for the results; these subordinates setting the objectives for their own subordinates and holding them accountable for the results, and so on), values are everyone’s responsibility and everyone can and should call out any other person violating them – including executives, and including customers and contractors in case the violation happened on the company’s premises.

关于最后一点，我们再补充一些。人们既要对取得业绩负责，也要对维护核心价值观负责。业绩的责任需要层层下达（首席执行官为其直接下属设定目标并要求他们对业绩负责；这些下属再为其下属设定目标并要求他们对业绩负责，以此类推），而价值观则是每个人的责任，每个人都可以而且应该指出任何违反价值观的人——包括高管，如果违规行为发生在公司场所，也包括客户和承包商。

# ↩


Always criticize behaviors, never people

总是批评行为，而不是批评人。

When calling out something wrong, managers should always direct the feedback or the critique towards a behavior of an employee, never to the employee himself.

当管理者指出员工的错误行为时，应该始终将反馈或批评指向员工的行为本身，而不是员工本人。

No one likes being criticized as a person . The reaction is likely to be anger, frustration or defensiveness. These emotions lead to ignoring the feedback at best, and to spreading demotivation amongst the team at worst.

没有人喜欢被人批评。人们的反应通常是愤怒、沮丧或辩解。这些情绪充其量会导致人们忽视反馈，最坏的情况则是打击团队士气。

Instead, people are generally open towards receiving feedback towards their behavior, especially if they believe that the person providing the feedback took some time to understand their point of view.

相反，人们通常乐于接受对其行为的反馈，尤其是当他们认为提供反馈的人花了一些时间去理解他们的观点时。

That’s why managers should always take a few seconds to observe the worker before initiating a discussion, and why they should ask “why were you doing that” before criticizing one of his behaviors. Asking before commenting will both provide the manager with valuable intelligence and will make the worker more likely to be open to feedback.

因此，管理者在与员工展开讨论之前，应该先花几秒钟观察一下，并在批评员工的某个行为之前先问问“你当时为什么这样做”。先询问后评论，既能为管理者提供宝贵的信息，也能让员工更愿意接受反馈。

Ask questions the right way

正确地提问

Managers should never ask questions from a point of arrogance, for doing so would only have negative consequences. Instead, managers should ask questions by giving the benefit of the doubt (perhaps there was a reason for the way the subordinate was behaving) but also being firm in refusing all excuses. In this context, every reason that does not require a procedure to be rewritten immediately or a disciplinary action towards someone else is an excuse.

管理者绝不应傲慢地提问，因为这样做只会带来负面后果。相反，管理者应该先给予下属信任（或许其行为有其原因），但同时也要坚决拒绝任何借口。在此语境下，任何无需立即修改流程或对他人采取纪律处分的理由都属于借口。

How questions are worded is very important. For example, I’ve noticed that asking questions such as “what would you change here?” is often replied with silence or indifferent comments such as “everything is fine here.” Instead, asking questions such as “if you were the line manager here, what would you change?” are usually answered with enthusiasm and intelligence.

提问的方式非常重要。例如，我注意到，问“你会在这里做出哪些改变？”这类问题，常常会得到沉默或冷漠的回应，比如“这里一切都很好”。相反，问“如果你是这里的直线经理，你会做出哪些改变？”这类问题，通常会得到热情而睿智的回答。

When asking questions, give your subordinates the authority to answer them.

提出问题时，要授权下属回答。

Communicating standards and priorities

沟通标准和优先事项

Management Walks, like the rest of performance management, are about communicating standards and priorities in a practical and unambiguous way.

管理巡视，就像绩效管理的其他方面一样，是为了以切实可行、明确无误的方式传达标准和优先事项。

Managers should keep this in mind at all times, never compromising on standards and priorities, especially during a Management Walk. That’s when the managers’ actions and priorities are the most visible.

管理者应始终牢记这一点，绝不能在标准和优先事项上妥协，尤其是在管理巡视期间。因为那时管理者的行为和优先事项最为显眼。

Script for a good Management Walk

一份优秀的管理层巡视脚本

The manager walks on the factory floor.

经理在工厂车间里走动。

He looks left and right and sees a worker performing some maintenance on a machine without a helmet.

他左右张望，看到一名工人在对机器进行维护时没有戴安全帽。

He spends a few seconds observing him.

他观察了他几秒钟。

He then walks towards him, signals his intention of speaking with him, and waits for him to come. (Better not to interrupt him too abruptly, unless in case of imminent danger. Abrupt interruptions might result in sudden reactions or losses of concentration which might themselves be dangerous.)

然后他朝他走去，示意他想和他说话，然后等着他过来。（最好不要太突然地打断他，除非有迫在眉睫的危险。突然打断可能会导致他做出突然的反应或注意力不集中，而这些本身就可能很危险。）

Manager: “Hi. Thank you for taking care of our machines.” (Begin with a thank you, if possible. It should be genuine, related to an actual reason for saying thank you.)

经理：“您好。感谢您维护我们的机器。”（如果可以，请以感谢开头。感谢要真诚，并说明感谢的实际原因。）

Manager: “I’ve noticed that you aren’t wearing the helmet. Is there any reason?” (Even if the rule is clear, the manager always tries to understand the worker’s point of view, both to gather information and to make the worker more open to feedback.)

经理：“我注意到你没戴头盔。有什么原因吗？”（即使规定很明确，经理也总是试图理解员工的观点，既是为了收集信息，也是为了让员工更容易接受反馈。）

Worker: “Oh, sorry, it’s just a two-minutes piece of work.”

工人：“哦，不好意思，这只是个两分钟就能完成的工作。”

Manager: “Two minutes might be enough to get an injury. Safety helmets must be always worn inside the factory. Your health is important.” (The manager reinforces the concept that rules are never to be broken, and Core Values such as safety are never to be compromised.)

经理：“两分钟就可能造成伤害。在工厂内必须始终佩戴安全帽。您的健康至关重要。”（经理强调规则绝对不能违反，安全等核心价值观绝对不能妥协。）

Manager: “Please wear a safety helmet on”. (The manager asks the worker to comply immediately – not next time.)

经理：“请戴上安全帽。”（经理要求工人立即遵守规定，而不是下次再做。）

Worker: “Okay.”

工人：“好的。”

The manager waits for the worker to go take a helmet and wear it. (The Manager shows that his words are always followed by action.)

经理等着工人去拿安全帽戴上。（经理的行为表明他言出必行。）

The worker is now wearing his helmet.

工人现在戴上了安全帽。

Manager: “Thank you for wearing the helmet. You’re an important member of your team and keeping you safe is in everyone’s best interest.” (Always thank the worker.)

经理：“谢谢你戴安全帽。你是团队的重要成员，保障你的安全符合每个人的利益。”（一定要感谢员工。）

Manager: “Is there anything else you’d like to discuss?” (Every interaction is an opportunity to gather intelligence.)

经理：“您还有什么想讨论的吗？”（每一次交流都是收集信息的机会。）

Script for a good Management Walk

一份优秀的管理层巡视脚本

The manager walks on the factory floor.

经理在工厂车间里走动。

He looks left and right and sees a few machinery components on the floor, where they should not be.

他左右环顾，发现地上散落着一些机器零件，这些零件不应该出现在那里。

He looks around and begins walking towards the closest worker, raising a hand to catch his attention.

他环顾四周，然后走向最近的工人，举起手引起他的注意。

Manager: “Hello. I’ve noticed that there are some components on the floor, blocking the walkway. Is there any reason?”

经理：“您好。我注意到地板上有一些零件，挡住了过道。请问是什么原因？”

Worker: “Mark just left them there temporarily, he will pick them up in an hour, when the rest of the components are ready.”

工人：“马克只是暂时把它们放在那里，一个小时后，等其他部件准备好了，他就会来取走它们。”

Manager: “I understand, but the walkway has to be left fully accessible at all times.” (The manager is inflexible and treats Core Values as priorities: never compromising on them.)

经理：“我明白，但走道必须始终保持畅通无阻。”（这位经理态度强硬，将核心价值观视为首要任务，绝不妥协。）

Manager: “Could you please put the components at their right place?”

经理：“请把这些部件放在正确的位置好吗？”

Worker: “I will tell Mark to do that as soon as possible.”

工人：“我会尽快告诉马克去做这件事。”

The manager looks around and sees that Mark is not in line of sight.

经理环顾四周，发现马克不在他的视线范围内。

Manager: “Please do it yourself now, it’s important. Safety is everyone’s priority.” (The manager does not risk that the worker forgets to tell Mark with the result of the components remaining there for long, telling everyone who sees them that components can be left out of place. Moreover, the manager reinforces the idea of peer accountability.)

经理：“请你现在就自己动手，这很重要。安全是每个人的首要任务。”（经理避免了工人忘记告诉马克，导致零件长时间堆放在那里，让所有看到的人都知道零件可以随意放置。此外，经理还强化了同事间相互负责的理念。）

The worker reluctantly moves the components to where they belong.

工人不情愿地将零件搬到了它们应该在的地方。

The manager helps him or watches him. Either way, once the worker is done, the manager thanks him.

经理要么帮他干活，要么看着他干。无论哪种方式，等工人干完活后，经理都会向他道谢。

Manager: “Thank you for helping to keep the plant safe and the rules respected. They are here for a reason, and we should never compromise them.” (The manager knows that the point of Management Walks is not only to spot what’s being done wrong, but more importantly to reinforce the importance of procedures and Core Values with visible and costly actions, such as spending a few minutes together with a worker to ensure that rules and procedures are respected.)

经理：“感谢你们协助维护工厂安全，并确保规章制度得到遵守。这些规章制度的存在是有原因的，我们绝不能违背它们。”（经理明白，管理巡视的目的不仅在于发现错误，更重要的是通过切实可见且成本高昂的行动来强化流程和核心价值观的重要性，例如花几分钟时间与员工交流，确保规章制度得到遵守。）

# ↩


Action points

行动要点

1) Create a schedule for your Management Walks: book a 30-minutes slot in your calendar once a month if you are a member of Top Management, once a week if you are a manager, and once a day if you are a supervisor.

1）制定管理巡视计划：如果您是高层管理人员，请每月在您的日历中预留 30 分钟；如果您是经理，请每周预留 30 分钟；如果您是主管，请每天预留 30 分钟。

2) If you are a manager or a member of Top Management, schedule a meeting with your subordinates in which you will ask them to implement Management Walks in their routine too. During the meeting, set unambiguous objectives on what constitutes a successful Management Walk (according to the First Principle of Operational Excellence) and describe how the objective will be evaluated (as per the Second Principle of Operational Excellence). I suggest that you accompany them during their first Management Walk, coaching them as they do it.

2) 如果您是经理或高层管理人员，请安排一次与下属的会议，要求他们将管理巡视融入日常工作中。会议期间，请明确定义一次成功的管理巡视应达到的目标（根据卓越运营的第一原则），并说明如何评估目标的实现情况（根据卓越运营的第二原则）。我建议您陪同他们进行第一次管理巡视，并在过程中提供指导。

Best Practice #2:
最佳实践#2：

Audits
审计

Audits are scripted Observation Walks. Instead of having the observer simply walk in an area and perform free observations, Audits use a checklist. Later in this chapter, you will find some examples.

审核是按照脚本进行的观察巡查。与让观察员随意在区域内走动进行自由观察不同，审核使用检查清单。本章稍后将提供一些示例。

The person performing the Audit walks in the area being audited with the checklist in his hand and, one by one, for each point of the checklist, it checks whether it is being observed or not. If it is observed, he marks it accordingly on the checklist and compliments a nearby worker for it. If it is not, he marks it as incomplete and interacts with a nearby worker as he would do during an Observation Walk.

审核员手持检查清单在审核区域内巡视，逐项检查清单上的每一项是否得到落实。如果落实到位，则在检查清单上做好相应标记，并对附近的员工表示表扬。如果未落实到位，则标记为“未完成”，并像在巡视观察中一样与附近的员工进行沟通。

At the end of the Audit, the checklist is sent to the supervisor of the area being audited and to the local HSE manager (even if just part of the audit covers safety). The result is annotated somewhere visible, such as a chart on a wall of the plant or of the office, where progress can be tracked.

审核结束后，检查清单会发送给被审核区域的主管和当地的健康、安全与环境（HSE）经理（即使审核仅涉及部分安全内容）。审核结果会标注在显眼的位置，例如工厂或办公室墙上的图表，以便跟踪进度。

Before going into the details of how an audit is performed, by whom and how often, let’s first see an example checklist.

在详细介绍审计的执行方式、执行人员和执行频率之前，我们先来看一个示例清单。

An example audit checklist

审计清单示例

The checklist below is purely for illustrative purposes. Each company should make their own so that it fits their own processes.

以下清单仅供参考。各公司应根据自身流程制定相应的清单。

Unsafe Habits: Is anyone going down the stairs without using the handrail? Is anyone without their PPEs (Personal Protective Equipment) (sub-checklist: helmet, glasses, gloves, mask, ear plugs / muffs, protective suit, safety shoes, harness, sensors, etc.?) Is anyone taking a shortcut? Is anyone performing maintenance on electrically powered installations without Lock-Out-Tag-Out (LOTO)?  Is anyone not wearing a seatbelt?

不安全习惯：有人下楼梯不扶扶手吗？有人没穿戴个人防护装备（PPE）（子清单：头盔、眼镜、手套、口罩、耳塞/耳罩、防护服、安全鞋、安全带、传感器等）吗？有人抄近路吗？有人在未进行上锁挂牌（LOTO）的情况下对电气设备进行维护吗？有人没系安全带吗？

Lack of focus: Is anyone multitasking?  Does anyone have his mobile phone in hand (when he shouldn’t)? Any signs of fatigue? Any signs of rushing? Any signs of frustration? Any opposing priorities?

注意力不集中：有人同时处理多项任务吗？有人不该玩手机的时候却拿着手机吗？有没有人表现出疲劳的迹象？有没有人表现得匆忙？有没有人表现出沮丧的情绪？有没有人分身乏术？

Disorder: Is 5S observed? [13] Is any tool out of place? Is any item in precarious equilibrium? Is any walkway missing clear boundaries? Is any walkway obstructed? Is any emergency exit obstructed? Is any fire extinguisher inaccessible? Is there any unprotected sharp surface? Is any area excessively dirty? Is the floor wet? Is the room too dark? Is any label missing?

混乱情况：是否遵守5S？[13] 是否有工具摆放不当？是否有物品处于摇摇欲坠的状态？是否有通道缺少清晰的边界？是否有通道被阻塞？是否有紧急出口被阻塞？是否有灭火器无法取用？是否有未加防护的尖锐表面？是否有区域过度脏污？地面是否潮湿？房间是否太暗？是否有标签缺失？

Tools: Is any tool inappropriate, deteriorated or broken? Is any tool misused? Is any tool unergonomic? Is any tool out of place or left in precarious equilibrium?

工具：是否有任何工具不合适、损坏或破损？是否有任何工具被误用？是否有任何工具不符合人体工程学？是否有任何工具放置不当或处于不稳固的平衡状态？

Procedures: Is any worker clearly not following the procedures? Is any work permit missing?

程序：是否有工人明显违反程序？是否有工作许可证缺失？

Audit: Did I thank the workers who are doing things properly? Did I interact with the workers who aren’t doing things properly? Did I have them take any corrective actions?

审核：我是否感谢了那些工作表现良好的员工？我是否与那些工作表现不佳的员工进行了沟通？我是否要求他们采取任何纠正措施？

As you will see, most of its items talk about Safety. This is intentional. As described in the chapter dedicated to the Third Principle, Safety is a leading indicator for Operation Excellence.

正如您所见，其中大部分内容都与安全有关。这是有意为之。正如专门论述第三原则的章节所述，安全是卓越运营的领先指标。

Who performs an Audit?

谁负责执行审计？

Audits should both be performed by Line Managers (they “own the area” and have the full technical knowledge and understanding to “see the most” during the Audit) and by all managers above Line Managers (to get them to spend time on the work floor and to familiarize them with the Operations of their own organization).

审计工作既应由一线经理执行（他们“负责该领域”，并且拥有充分的技术知识和理解，可以在审计过程中“看到最多”），也应由一线经理以上的各级经理执行（以便让他们花时间在工作现场，并熟悉自己组织的运作）。

How often should Audits be performed?

审计应该多久进行一次？

Line Managers should perform an Audit at least once every month. This goes in addition to performing at least one Management Walk per week.

各部门经理应至少每月进行一次审计。此外，每周还应至少进行一次管理巡视。

Higher management should perform at least one Audit a quarter, in addition to performing at least one Management Walk per month.

高层管理人员除了每月至少进行一次管理巡视外，还应至少每季度进行一次审计。

Audits are always complementary to Management Walks, not alternatives. The checklist used in the Audit is a tool to make sure that the important conditions and behaviors are spotted, but it might constrain observation and prevent the auditor from noticing things outside the checklist. Hence the importance of performing both Management Walks and Audits.

审计始终是对管理巡视的补充，而非替代。审计中使用的检查清单是确保发现重要情况和行为的工具，但它可能会限制观察范围，使审计人员无法注意到检查清单之外的情况。因此，管理巡视和审计同时进行至关重要。

It might seem too much, but this is a book about achieving Operational Excellence, not about attempting it.

这或许看起来有点夸张，但这本书讲的是如何实现卓越运营，而不是如何尝试实现卓越运营。

When Audits fail

审计失败时

In my experience, Audits fail when they become inconsequential, when they represent a checklist to go through and nothing more.

根据我的经验，当审计变得无关紧要，仅仅沦为一份需要逐项核对的清单时，审计就会失败。

In order to be effective, performing Audits should become a personal objective of anyone required to perform them, with the same significance of output-related objectives.

为了有效开展审计工作，执行审计工作应该成为每个被要求执行审计工作的人员的个人目标，其重要性与产出相关目标相当。

If you are a manager, you should give your subordinates personal objectives on Audits performed and follow them once in a while on the field while they do them or talk with the workers affected to probe the quality of the Audits and ensure they are effective. As mentioned during the discussion of the Second Principle of Operational Excellence, while you are giving your subordinates the personal objective of Audits, do not forget them to set a clear standard for what a successful Audit looks like and how you will evaluate them.

如果您是管理者，您应该为下属设定个人审计目标，并定期到现场监督他们的工作，或与相关员工交谈，以了解审计质量并确保其有效性。正如在讨论卓越运营第二原则时提到的，在为下属设定审计个人目标的同时，不要忘记为他们设定明确的成功审计标准以及评估方法。

Action points

行动要点

1) On Word, Excel, Google Docs, or a similar software, create an Audit checklist for the office or plant where your subordinates work at.

1）在 Word、Excel、Google Docs 或类似软件中，为你的下属工作的办公室或工厂创建一份审核清单。

2) If you are a Line Manager or Supervisor, book in your calendar a monthly 30-minutes slot in which to perform the Audit. If you are a Manager, schedule a meeting with your subordinates in which you will ask them to perform regular Audits (make sure that you set clear expectations as per the First and Second Principle of Operational Excellence, and make sure that you consistently evaluate their performance at Audits as per the Fourth Principle of Operational Excellence).

2) 如果您是直线经理或主管，请在您的日程表中预留每月 30 分钟的时间进行审核。如果您是经理，请安排与您的下属开会，要求他们定期进行审核（请确保您根据卓越运营的第一和第二原则设定明确的期望，并确保您根据卓越运营的第四原则持续评估他们在审核中的表现）。

3) Book a 30-minutes slot in your schedule 3 months from now in which you will evaluate your auditing process, making any necessary adjustment to the process. If you are a manager, invite your subordinates.

3）请在三个月后的日程安排中预留30分钟时间，用于评估您的审计流程，并根据需要进行调整。如果您是经理，请邀请您的下属参加。
