纳西姆·尼古拉斯·塔勒布的《风险承担》一书阐述了为什么必须完全追究责任。

The Control Heuristic, 2 nd Edition” , by Luca Dellanna (myself), on why changing habits is so hard.

《控制启发式》（第二版），作者 Luca Dellanna（本人），探讨了为什么改变习惯如此困难。

“The Four Obsessions of an Extraordinary Executive” , by Patrick Lencioni, though his other books on leadership are excellent too.

帕特里克·兰西奥尼的《一位杰出高管的四大执念》一书非常出色，不过他其他关于领导力的著作也同样优秀。

“The Hard Thing About Hard Things” , by Silicon Valley entrepreneur Ben Horowitz, on the challenges of being a CEO.

《创业维艰》（The Hard Thing About Hard Things），硅谷企业家本·霍洛维茨（Ben Horowitz）著，讲述了担任首席执行官所面临的挑战。

“The Power of Adaptation ” , by Luca Dellanna (myself), for practical tips on how organizations can and should adapt to an everchanging environment.

《适应的力量》，作者 Luca Dellanna（本人），提供了一些关于组织如何以及应该如何适应不断变化的环境的实用技巧。

The books in this list are sorted by alphabetical order.

此列表中的书籍按字母顺序排列。

# ↩

Highlights

精彩片段

From the First Principle of Operational Excellence

从卓越运营的第一原则出发

When a manager fails to execute on performance management, he compromises the good results he might have obtained in other areas.

当一位经理未能有效执行绩效管理时，他会损害他在其他领域可能取得的良好成果。

The more ambiguous an objective, the higher the chances that a worker misinterprets it and fails to fulfill it. Lack of clarity makes it challenging for managers to hold their subordinates accountable.

目标越模糊，员工误解目标并导致无法完成目标的可能性就越高。缺乏清晰的目标会使管理者难以追究下属的责任。

Managers who set ambiguous objectives tend to have underperforming subordinates and are less likely to hold them accountable for their underperformance.

目标不明确的管理者往往会有表现不佳的下属，而且不太可能追究他们的责任。

Once a manager has let someone off the hook, he sets a precedent for others, making it easier for them to argue they should also be given a pass. This makes it even more difficult in the future for the manager to be consistent in the application of consequences and further deteriorates the operational culture of the team.

一旦经理放过某人，就等于开了先例，让其他人更容易为自己辩解，认为自己也应该得到宽恕。这使得经理未来更难在执行惩罚措施时保持一致性，并进一步恶化团队的运营文化。

Managers who set unclear and unambitious objectives cannot reward those employees who performed and cannot punish those who didn’t. Consequently, the team underperforms.

管理者如果设定的目标不明确且缺乏挑战性，就无法奖励表现出色的员工，也无法惩罚表现不佳的员工。结果，团队绩效低下。

Good managers are aware of the vicious circle of bad performance management. They prevent it by setting clear objectives and by being fully consistent in applying consequences.

优秀的管理者深知糟糕的绩效管理会形成恶性循环。他们会通过设定清晰的目标并始终如一地执行相应的惩罚措施来避免这种情况的发生。

When managers fail to set clear objectives, it is not because of a lack of skills. Rather, it is because of some mental patterns of theirs that makes them believe that setting unclear objectives is the optimal choice.

管理者未能设定清晰目标，并非因为他们缺乏能力，而是因为他们的一些思维模式让他们误以为设定模糊的目标才是最佳选择。

Guilt and shame by a manager are symptoms of insufficient clarity, individuality or ambitiousness during delegation.

管理者感到内疚和羞愧，是其在授权过程中缺乏清晰的思路、个性或雄心的表现。

Good managers do not wait for the perfect environment for them to do their work; rather, they realize that it’s their job to create a conducive environment.

优秀的管理者不会等待完美的环境来开展工作；相反，他们意识到创造一个有利的环境是他们的职责。

When good managers spot a lack of motivation in their subordinates, they interpret it as a signal of a lack of clarity of objectives, of personal impact or of individual outcomes.

优秀的管理者发现下属缺乏积极性时，会将其解读为目标不明确、个人影响力不足或个人成果不够清晰的信号。

It is helpful and generous to set clear and ambitious objectives and to guarantee fair consequences. Conversely, it is those managers that are ambiguous in the definition of objectives and inconsistent in the application of consequences that are selfish. In order to feel more comfortable with themselves, they limit the potential of their subordinates.

设定清晰且富有挑战性的目标，并保证公平的后果，这既有益又慷慨。相反，那些目标定义含糊不清、惩罚措施执行前后不一致的管理者，则是自私的。为了让自己感觉更舒服，他们限制了下属的潜力。

Chronically requiring overtime is a sign of a dysfunctional company which tries to compensate its structural problems by burdening its employees.

长期要求员工加班是公司运作失灵的标志，该公司试图通过加重员工负担来弥补其结构性问题。

Chronically making overtime is a sign of a dysfunctional manager who tries to cover his effectiveness problem with throwing more time and energy at problems which do not need it.

长期加班是管理不善的标志，这种管理者试图通过投入更多的时间和精力来解决并不需要投入更多时间精力的问题来掩盖其工作效率低下的问题。

Indifference and laziness are symptoms of having forgotten that good outcomes follow good performance.

冷漠和懒惰是忘记了好的表现会带来好的结果的症状。

The manager has to create the conditions to be able to “catch the subordinate doing something good”.

管理者必须创造条件，才能“发现下属的优秀表现”。

Bad managers try to reach alignment through communication; good managers achieve alignment by rewarding the behaviors which are aligned with the objectives of the organization.

糟糕的管理者试图通过沟通来达成共识；优秀的管理者通过奖励与组织目标相符的行为来达成共识。

Whenever a manager takes the “easy choice” and sacrifices clarity, fairness or consistency to avoid a difficult conversation or a difficult choice, he incurs “management debt”: a subjective short-term gain which will eventually have to be paid back with interest.

每当一位经理为了避免艰难的谈话或艰难的选择而选择“最简单的做法”，牺牲清晰度、公平性或一致性时，他就会背负“管理债务”：一种主观的短期收益，最终必须连本带利地偿还。

The more the manager takes “easy choices” by sacrificing clarity, fairness or consistency, the more his subordinates will take “easy choices” themselves by sacrificing performance, quality and teamwork.

经理越是选择“容易的选择”，牺牲清晰度、公平性或一致性，他的下属就越会选择“容易的选择”，牺牲绩效、质量和团队合作。

From the Second Principle of Operational Excellence

来自卓越运营的第二原则

Your subordinates cannot do what is required from them unless, after you provide them with the tools, you release your grip on them.

除非你给下属提供必要的工具，然后放开对他们的控制，否则他们无法完成你要求他们做的事情。

Prescribing methods removes accountability, whereas prescribing results enable it.

按方法开处方会消除问责制，而按结果开处方则可以实现问责制。

A manager should only prescribe the instructions and boundaries as part of the result, never as the result itself.

管理者应该只将指令和界限作为结果的一部分来规定，而绝不能将其作为结果本身。

If you delegate tasks other than problems, you’re basically crossing fingers on whether completing the task will achieve meaningful results.

如果你委派的任务不是解决问题，那么你基本上就是在祈祷完成任务后能否取得有意义的结果。

In great companies, objectives are tricked down from the CEO and accountability for a given objective is owned by everyone on the hierarchical line from the CEO to each employee whose actions might influence that objective.

在伟大的公司里，目标是由首席执行官自上而下传达的，而对于特定目标的责任则由层级上的每个人承担，从首席执行官到每个可能影响该目标的员工。

Good managers paint visual, explicit, unequivocal, clear descriptions of what a good result looks like.

优秀的管理者会用形象、明确、清晰、毫不含糊的语言描述好的结果是什么样子。

In industries in which processes and technologies change very fast, a manager who thinks he knows the job of his subordinates quickly becomes a hindrance to the performance of his team.

在流程和技术快速变化的行业中，如果一位管理者自认为了解下属的工作，很快就会成为团队绩效的阻碍。

Whereas objectives must be set from some level of overview, the decisions related to how to complete them are complex and require specific, fast-changing, low-level local knowledge. Therefore, great companies strive to have decisions taken at the lowest competent level.

目标的设定必须基于一定的宏观层面，但如何实现这些目标的决策却十分复杂，需要具体、瞬息万变的基层本地知识。因此，优秀的公司力求让决策在最基层、最有能力的人员层面做出。

Accountability is not the result of motivation, but its cause.

问责制不是动机的结果，而是动机的原因。

Managers do not have to motivate employees. Rather, they must prevent the conditions that might lead to them becoming demotivated.

管理者不必激励员工，而应该防止可能导致员工失去积极性的情况发生。

In order to reach an unwavering level of explicitness and clarity, good managers are relentless in making the implicit explicit, even when doing so would seem an insult to the intelligence of their interlocutor.

为了达到毫不动摇的明确性和清晰度，优秀的管理者会坚持不懈地将隐含的信息明确化，即使这样做似乎是对谈话者智商的侮辱。

Good managers never assume an attitude which signals that they own the tasks they delegate.

优秀的管理者绝不会摆出一副认为自己对委派的任务拥有所有权的态度。

Good managers are explicit about how results will be evaluated and by whom. The reason is not only to make the goal clearer, but foremost to prevent surprises and frustration by subordinates who might think they have been unfairly judged. (“Unfairly” is often a synonym with “a rule not stated in advance”).

优秀的管理者会明确说明如何评估业绩以及由谁来评估。这样做不仅是为了使目标更清晰，更重要的是为了避免下属感到意外和沮丧，认为他们受到了不公平的评价。（“不公平”通常等同于“事先未说明的规则”）。

From the Third Principle of Operational Excellence

来自卓越运营的第三项原则

The reason why Core Values are so difficult to adopt in the day-to-day of Operations is that they represent short-term costs.

核心价值观之所以难以在日常运营中得到贯彻，是因为它们代表着短期成本。

Good managers know that one of the reasons that employees do not practice Core Values is because they are fearful of potential punishments for not having been productive in the short-term. Therefore, they personally take visible actions incurring these costs, to show that they are truly worth paying.

优秀的管理者深知，员工不践行核心价值观的原因之一是害怕短期内因业绩不佳而受到惩罚。因此，他们会亲自采取切实行动，承担相应的成本，以此证明这些付出是值得的。

Good managers use both words and actions. The costlier the action, the stronger its effect towards getting Core Values internalized.

优秀的管理者言行一致。行动成本越高，对核心价值观的内化效果就越好。

Culture is not made of perks and terminology, but of time- and cost-expensive rituals which are conspicuously perceived as worth it.

文化不是由特权和术语构成的，而是由耗时耗力的仪式构成的，这些仪式被人们明显地认为是值得的。

From the Fourth Principle of Operational Excellence

来自卓越运营的第四项原则

Bad managers are volatile in the application of the standards they set. They believe that workers respond to the average application of the standard. Instead, workers remember the extremes.

糟糕的管理者在执行他们制定的标准时往往摇摆不定。他们认为员工会对标准的平均执行情况做出反应。然而，员工记住的往往是极端情况。

Consistent judgment on unambiguous objectives whose specifics have been clear since the beginning cannot be unfair.

对从一开始就明确无误的目标做出始终如一的判断，不可能是不公平的。

If managers reward effort, eventually, their subordinates will spend their time showing effort rather than getting results.

如果管理者奖励的是努力，那么最终，他们的下属会把时间花在努力上，而不是取得成果上。

Good managers set targets high enough that their completion brings enough windfall to be redistributed across their team.

优秀的管理者会设定足够高的目标，这样完成目标后就能获得足够的收益，可以重新分配给团队成员。

Good managers understand that failing to notice that the work was subpar will, counterintuitively, lead to their best team members getting demotivated.

优秀的管理者明白，如果未能注意到工作质量不达标，反而会导致团队中最优秀的成员失去动力。

Good managers are fair and loyal to principles, not loyal to people.

优秀的管理者公正且忠于原则，而不是忠于人。

From the rest of the book

本书其余部分

It’s not that most managers do not reward achieving objectives. They do. However, often, they do it less consistently that they let having achieved objectives go unrewarded. Unfortunately, people are more likely to remember that one time where their efforts went to waste rather than those nine times where they got rewarded.

并非大多数管理者不奖励达成目标的员工。他们确实会奖励。然而，他们往往奖励得不够及时，以至于有些达成目标的员工最终却得不到奖励。不幸的是，人们更容易记住那一次努力付诸东流的经历，而不是那九次获得奖励的经历。

Your main tasks as a manager are making the important unmistakable and conspicuous, and consistently rewarding people based on their result against their personal objectives and on stewarding Core Values.

作为管理者，你的主要任务是使重要的事情明确无误、引人注目，并根据员工实现个人目标的成果和对核心价值观的践行，持续地给予奖励。

Do not assume that your subordinates already know how their efforts contribute to others, and do not assume that telling them is an insult to their intelligence. People need to be explicitly reminded of the worth of their efforts, even if they know it already.

不要想当然地认为你的下属已经明白他们的努力对他人有何贡献，也不要认为告诉他们是在侮辱他们的智商。即使人们已经知道，也需要被明确地提醒他们自己努力的价值。

As a manager, it is both your job to help your subordinates understand the meaning of their work and to ensure that they are, in turn, helping their own subordinates do the same.

作为管理者，你的职责既是帮助下属理解工作的意义，也是确保他们反过来帮助他们的下属理解工作的意义。

Decisions taken in the managers’ office remain in there. They do not have the power to affect the way of working of their subordinates unless the manager translates them into visible actions at their subordinates’ workplace.

经理办公室里做出的决定仅限于办公室内部。除非经理将这些决定转化为下属工作场所中可见的行动，否则它们无权影响下属的工作方式。

Either the rule or procedure has to be rewritten, or the worker has to acknowledge he shouldn’t have acted that way. There is no grey area in between, no one-off exception. Letting an exception pass once is how exceptions become the new norm. Good managers never allow that.

要么修改规则或流程，要么员工必须承认自己不应该那样做。没有中间地带，也没有例外。放任例外一次，例外就会变成新的常态。优秀的管理者绝不会允许这种情况发生。

Holding peers, subordinates and superiors accountable for rules, standards and Core Values is everyone’s responsibility.

让同事、下属和上级对规则、标准和核心价值观负责，是每个人的责任。

When calling out something wrong, managers should always direct the feedback or the critique towards a behavior of an employee. Never to the employee himself.

当管理者指出员工的错误时，应该始终将反馈或批评针对员工的行为本身，而绝不能针对员工本人。

When asking questions, give your subordinates the authority to answer them.

提出问题时，要授权下属回答。

The main function of Weekly Meetings is to reinforce the Core Values and Operational Culture of the organization.

每周例会的主要功能是强化组织的核心价值观和运营文化。

People need to be repeated the importance of whatever is not the default state, for they for they progressively revert back to it otherwise.

需要不断向人们强调非默认状态的重要性，否则他们会逐渐恢复到默认状态。

Good managers know that, no matter how many times Core Values have been mentioned during Weekly Meetings, if during a single Weekly Meeting they are not mentioned, doubt regarding their importance and uncompromisability will rise again in its attendees.

优秀的管理者都知道，无论在每周例会上提到核心价值观多少次，如果在某次每周例会上没有提到核心价值观，与会者就会再次对其重要性和不可妥协性产生怀疑。

Weekly meetings are exceptional tools for communication because the manager has the opportunity to talk to his whole team at the same time. Each attendee will know that whatever expectation has been set during the meeting, each other attendee heard it as well.

每周例会是绝佳的沟通工具，因为管理者有机会同时与全体团队成员交流。每位参会者都能清楚地知道，会议期间提出的任何要求，其他参会者也都听到了。

Conspicuousness – setting expectations in a way which is visible to everyone – is a great way to effectively influence the actions of others.

显眼性——以人人都能看到的方式设定期望——是有效影响他人行为的好方法。

Good managers do not only communicate to get every subordinate to know and embrace what has to be done; they also communicate to make sure that every subordinate knows that everyone else in the team knows and embraces what has to be done. Weekly meetings are a great channel to do that.

优秀的管理者不仅会通过沟通让每位下属了解并接受需要完成的任务，还会确保每位下属都明白团队中的其他成员也了解并接受需要完成的任务。每周例会是实现这一目标的绝佳途径。

If any comment is made upon someone’s personality, the manager should immediately refocus it on someone’s behavior.

如果有人对某人的性格发表评论，经理应该立即将注意力转移到该人的行为上。

Before the meeting ends, the manager has to make sure that every single participant will walk out the door committed to do whatever task has been assigned to him during the meeting, even if he did not agree about it.

在会议结束前，经理必须确保每一位参会者都能带着完成会议期间分配给他的任何任务的决心离开会议室，即使他并不同意这项任务。

Ideally, meetings should follow the “disagree and commit” model.

理想情况下，会议应遵循“求同存异”的模式。

It is critical that a supervisor that walks out the meeting communicates to his team the right things in the right way.

至关重要的是，一位主管在会后走出会议室时，要以正确的方式向他的团队传达正确的信息。

Passive commitment is equal to passive sabotage.

消极承诺等同于消极破坏。

Great managers demand conflict (by asking everyone to voice their concerns), then demand commitment (by asking everyone to promise what they will do) and finally demand results (by letting everyone know that they will be held accountable for doing whatever the team decided).

优秀的管理者会先要求产生冲突（让每个人都表达自己的担忧），然后要求做出承诺（让每个人都承诺自己会做什么），最后要求取得成果（让每个人都知道，无论团队做出什么决定，他们都要为此负责）。

One-on-one Meetings should last at least half an hour, even if there is nothing to discuss, especially if there is nothing to discuss. This because there is never nothing to discuss.

一对一会谈至少应持续半小时，即便没有什么可谈的，尤其是没有什么可谈的时候。因为总会有可谈的。

Buffers prevent problems to surface, until it’s too late. Just In Time (and other techniques which reduce buffers) allow problems to surface so that they can be solved before it’s too late.

缓冲机制会阻止问题显现，直到为时已晚。而即时生产（以及其他减少缓冲机制的技术）则允许问题显现，以便在为时过晚之前得到解决。

Problems grow the size they need in order to be acknowledged. An organization that is slow in acknowledging problems will find itself with big problems.

问题只有发展到一定程度才会被人重视。一个组织如果迟迟不肯正视问题，最终只会陷入更大的麻烦。

Measuring trends at the bottom of the pyramid allows to be proactive and to prevent negative events; measuring trends at the top causes to be reactive and to suffer from negative events.

衡量金字塔底部的趋势可以让我们积极主动地预防负面事件；而衡量金字塔顶部的趋势则会导致我们被动应对，从而遭受负面事件的打击。

By tying consequences (rewards and punishments) to leading indicators in addition to lagging ones, the frequency of negative events increases, causing the incentive to optimize for the frequent small profits to disappear.

通过将后果（奖励和惩罚）与领先指标以及滞后指标联系起来，负面事件的发生频率会增加，从而导致追求频繁小额利润的动机消失。

If a bad performance on a lagging indicator does not impact the employee in any way, then he will not change his behavior.

如果滞后指标表现不佳不会对员工产生任何影响，那么他就不会改变自己的行为。

Shortcuts are the shortest way to another instance of the same problem.

走捷径是导致再次出现相同问题的最短途径。

Incident investigations are as effective as the level of the highest person involved.

事件调查的有效性取决于最高负责人的水平。

Some managers dismiss the importance of poster by saying that their subordinates already know what’s written on them. These managers forget that Communication doesn’t happen when a message is first said; it happens when it cannot be mistaken anymore.

有些管理者轻视海报的重要性，认为下属都知道海报上的内容。这些管理者忘记了，沟通并非发生在信息被说出的那一刻，而是发生在信息不再被误解的那一刻。

Labels (and visual aids in general) are not there to protect against inexperience. They are there to protect against fatigue, rushing, and other mental conditions which might cause an otherwise competent operator to commit a mistake.

标签（以及一般的视觉辅助工具）并非为了防止经验不足，而是为了防止疲劳、匆忙以及其他可能导致原本合格的操作人员犯错的精神状态。

Great companies do not only use visual aids for things that are hard to remember; they use them for things which are important to remember, regardless of whether they’re obvious or not.

优秀的公司不仅会使用视觉辅助工具来帮助记忆难以记住的事情，还会将其用于需要记住的重要事情，无论这些事情是否显而易见。

In my experience, the main predictor for whether an initiative will succeed is whether it achieved critical mass: whether, in at least a location (a team, a production line, a plant, an office floor, etc.), at least 80-90% of the people are exhibiting the desired behaviors.

根据我的经验，一项举措能否成功的主要预测因素是它是否达到了临界规模：至少在某个地方（一个团队、一条生产线、一个工厂、一个办公楼层等），至少 80-90% 的人是否表现出了期望的行为。

“No [team] has time to do optional things. Therefore, training must be mandatory.” – Ben Horowitz

“任何球队都没有时间去做可有可无的事情。因此，训练必须是强制性的。”——本·霍洛维茨

The more an employee is towards the right of the Adoption Curve spectrum, the higher the percentage of his colleagues who need to adopt the procedure for him to be willing to do so. Therefore, managers of large divisions who focus their energy towards all subordinates at the same time in the same way are bound to fail. Instead, change initiatives must be progressively rolled out. First, to innovators. Then, to the early majority. Only afterwards, to the majority of the team. The adoption of the former two groups is needed to recruit the latter one.

员工在采纳曲线上的位置越靠右，他需要接受该流程的同事比例就越高，他才会愿意接受。因此，大型部门的管理者如果试图同时以同样的方式向所有下属集中精力，注定会失败。相反，变革举措必须循序渐进地推行。首先是创新者，然后是早期大众，最后才是团队的大多数成员。前两类群体的采纳是争取最后一批成员的前提。

Great companies exhibit the following two traits. First, they keep talking about the Four Principles of Operational Excellence even when they do not seem necessary anymore. Second, they keep placing costly objectives on the achievement of Core Values based goals.

优秀的公司具备以下两个特点。首先，即使不再必要，他们仍然会反复强调卓越运营的四大原则。其次，他们不断设定高成本的目标，以实现基于核心价值观的目标。

Instead of conducting exit interviews asking people who left your team why they did so, ask them these questions while they still are your team members.

与其在离职面谈中询问离开团队的人为什么离开，不如在他们还是团队成员的时候就问他们这些问题。

Only institutionalized Culture lasts.

只有制度化的文化才能长久存在。

The 1 st Principle  of Operational Excellence:
卓越运营的第一原则：
Good managers set unambiguous, individual and rewardable objectives
优秀的管理者会设定明确、个性化且可奖励的目标

The 2nd Principle  of Operational Excellence:
卓越运营的第二原则：
Good managers always explicitly assign full accountability together with objectives
优秀的管理者总是明确地将全部责任与目标结合起来。

The 3rd Principle  of Operational Excellence:
卓越运营的第三项原则：
Good managers demonstrate priorities with visible costly actions
优秀的管理者会通过可见的、代价高昂的行动来展现优先事项。

The 4th Principle  of Operational Excellence:
卓越运营的第四原则：
Good managers are obsessively consistent in holding their subordinates accountable
优秀的管理者会始终如一地要求下属承担责任。

[18] One particularly nasty type of shortcut is reducing volatility in non-Gaussian environments by skewing the frequency and intensity of problems to the right (e.g., undertaking behaviors that have positive payoff most of the time and negative payoff very few times but when such negative payoffs occur, the survival of the company becomes endangered). Great companies reduce volatility without using shortcuts (i.e., they look for a real decrease in volatility, not an increase in skewedness) while still keeping redundancy and flexibility.

[18] 一种特别糟糕的捷径是通过将问题发生的频率和强度向右偏移来降低非高斯环境下的波动性（例如，采取大多数情况下收益为正、极少情况下收益为负的行为，但一旦出现负收益，公司的生存就会受到威胁）。优秀的公司在不走捷径的情况下降低波动性（也就是说，他们追求的是波动性的真正降低，而不是偏度的增加），同时还能保持冗余性和灵活性。
